docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Item LDM is the standard, governed logical interface for eBay item-domain data, abstracting fragmented underlying physical sources to enable self-service consumption on GDS platform to support business use cases such as data engineering, analytics, and ML feature engineering.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
Understanding Item domain fundamentals:

  • Item, Variation, Product

    Core entity hierarchy: listings (item), SKUs (variation), and catalog references (product/ePID)

  • Attributes vs Aspects

    Two ways to describe items: seller-provided attributes vs SAP-processed aspects with higher quality

  • Variation Traits

    SKU-level differentiators like Color, Size, Network that distinguish variations

Learn core concepts in detail →

docs.title: LDM Relationships and Lifecycle
docs.text:
The catalog contains two LDM types:

  • Governed LDMs provide the consumer-facing item and variation models.
  • Raw LDMs represent source data and behavior. They are grouped according to the source and site application model design.

The relationships below explain how the raw-LDM groups support the listing lifecycle, rather than describing relational-table joins.

docs.title: Current Listing State
docs.text: The governed item and variation entities represent a listing and its SKU-level variations. Their raw current-state data is held in ItemKeyspace. ItemRoot contains the identity and broad state for one item or variation. ItemCompatibility, ItemDescription, ItemPriceAndQuantity, ItemDetails, and ItemBusinessPolicies are separate raw LDMs, allowing those portions of the listing to be read and updated independently. ItemLock records one or more inventory reservations for the item. ItemUUIDMapping is a seller-and-UUID lookup that resolves a listing.

docs.title: Shared MSKU State
docs.text: ItemGroupKeyspace holds data shared by the variations in an MSKU listing. ItemGroupRoot identifies the group and references its member items, while ItemGroupDescription and ItemGroupBusinessPolicies hold the shared description and policies. The group does not replace the current state of its member variations: their sellable price, quantity, lifecycle, and other item-specific data remain in ItemKeyspace.

docs.title: Draft Listing State
docs.text: ListingDraft is an independent working-state group used before or during publication. ListingDraftRoot stores draft-session state. An SSKU draft contains ListingDraftItem and can include ListingDraftItemCompatibility. An MSKU draft contains ListingDraftGroup, ListingDraftGroupDescription, and optionally ListingDraftGroupCompatibility, plus one ListingDraftItem for each variation. Draft LDMs do not imply that a corresponding live ItemKeyspace or ItemGroupKeyspace record exists.

docs.title: Active Draft Discovery
docs.text: UserListingDraftMap is a user-scoped index of active drafts. It connects a user and a draft identifier to summary metadata used to find the draft, but does not contain the full ListingDraft content. Its lifecycle is separate from the draft content: creating, updating, or deleting one does not automatically change the other.

docs.title: Listing Revision History
docs.text: ListingRevisionKeyspace stores historical changes by listing identifier, separately from current state. ListingRevisionRoot is optional retention state. Each ListingRevision records a revision summary and can have multiple ListingRevisionDetail children for listing-property changes and ListingVariationRevisionDetail children for variation-property changes. These LDMs are history records and do not replace the latest ItemKeyspace or ItemGroupKeyspace data.

docs.title: Access Methods
docs.text:
Spark SQLDDF Python

Query via Spark SQL on DLS:

-- Example: Query active US listings in a specific category
SELECT 
    item_id,
    auct_titl             AS title,
    bin_price_lstg_curncy AS price,
    leaf_categ_id,
    slr_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0
  AND leaf_categ_id = 9355
  AND bin_price_lstg_curncy > 100
LIMIT 100;

Programmatic access via Declarative Data Flow (DDF): Examples to be added.

Migrating from Legacy Hive Tables?

Currently using DW_LSTG_ITEM, DW_ATTR_DETAIL_VALUES, or other legacy tables? See the Migration Guide for step-by-step instructions to migrate your queries to Item Domain LDM.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text: Understanding the foundational concepts in the Item domain.

docs.title: Item
docs.text:
Item

Definition: A listing on eBay's platform. In the data warehouse, item_id (also known as listing_id) uniquely identifies each item.

Characteristics:

  • Can be single-SKU (SSKU) or multi-SKU (MSKU)
  • Contains seller-provided metadata (title, price, description, category)
  • Has attributes (seller input) and aspects (SAP-generated)

Example:

"Apple iPhone 17 Pro for (AT&T or Cricket) - New Open Box, Never Used"

  • Item ID: 227255267188
  • Price: $1,029.99

  • Attributes: Brand=Apple, Condition=Open Box, Processor=A19 Pro, Style=Smartphone, etc

docs.title: Variation
docs.text:
Variation

Definition: A specific SKU within a multi-variation listing, reflecting different product configurations.

Characteristics:

  • Only exists for MSKU items
  • Has variation traits (characteristics that differ across SKUs)
  • Each variation has its own price, quantity, SKU

Example:

For the iPhone listing above, variations might include:

  • Variation 1: Network=AT&T, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue
  • Variation 2: Network=T-Mobile, Storage=512GB, Color=Silver
  • Variation 3: Network=Verizon, Storage=1TB, Color=Orange

Variation Traits: Network, Storage Capacity, Color

docs.title: Product
docs.text:
Product

Definition: Product catalog reference (ePID - eBay Product ID) that groups items representing the same physical entity.

Types:

  • Seller-tagged (PROD_REF_ID): Seller manually assigns ePID during listing creation
  • Auto-tagged (AT_PROD_REF_ID): eBay's Structured Data Adoption team assigns ePID

Relationship:

  • Multiple items (different sellers, conditions, prices) → Same product (ePID)
  • Enables cross-listing analysis and product catalog mapping

Example:

ePID 285507661 = "iPhone 15 Pro" → Links all iPhone 15 Pro listings regardless of seller

docs.title: Entity Relationships
docs.text:
• One item can have 0 to many variations (1:N)
  • Multiple items reference the same product via ePID (N:1)

docs.title: Attributes vs Aspects
docs.text:
Two ways to describe item characteristics. The core difference lies in data source and quality:

Attribute vs Aspect Comparison

Dimension Attribute Aspect Data Source Seller input Processed from attributes by SAP (Search Annotation Platform) Data Quality Raw data, inconsistent format Cleaned, standardized, enriched Generation Seller provides when creating listing SAP extracts, normalizes, and standardizes from attributes Primary Use View Item Page display, basic filtering Search indexing, recommendations, high-precision classification Visibility Buyer-facing (shown on product page) Internal eBay systems (search, recommendation) Example Brand=apple, Storage=256 GB, Color=dark blue Brand=Apple, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue, Screen_Size=6.3" Storage EAV pattern Structured taxonomy with namespace/classifier IDs Tables dw_attr_detail_values, dw_attr_lstg_dtl, dw_attr_shpmt_dtl item_aspct_clssfctn_sap, vrtn_aspct_clssfctn_sap

Why do we need Aspects?

Seller-provided attributes have inconsistent quality (typos, format variations, missing information), which cannot meet the precision requirements of search and recommendation systems. SAP generates high-quality aspects through:

  • Normalization: apple → Apple, 256 GB → 256GB (via UNS - Unified Normalization Service)
  • Enrichment: Extract missing attributes from title/description (e.g., Screen Size, OS)
  • Standardization: Map to unified names/values using UMS (Unified Metadata System)

Real-world Example

Seller-provided Attributes: 

Brand=apple, Storage=256 GB, Color=dark blue

SAP-generated Aspects: 

Brand=Apple, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue, 
Screen_Size=6.3", Operating_System=iOS, Camera_Resolution=48MP

Notice how aspects are standardized and include additional information extracted from the listing.

docs.title: Variation Traits
docs.text:
Traits

Definition: Variation-level characteristics that differentiate SKUs within the same multi-SKU item.

Characteristics:

  • Only exist for MSKU items with variations
  • Describe the specific features that differ across variations
  • Common trait types: Color, Size, Style, Capacity, Network, Material

Purpose:

  • Enable SKU differentiation within the same listing
  • Support variation-level analysis (e.g., which color/size sells better)
  • Help buyers select the specific variant they want

Examples:

For a clothing item with multiple variations:

  • Traits: Color (Red, Blue, Black), Size (S, M, L, XL)
  • Variation 1: Color=Red, Size=S
  • Variation 2: Color=Blue, Size=M
  • Variation 3: Color=Black, Size=L

For a smartphone listing:

  • Traits: Network (AT&T, Verizon, Unlocked), Storage (128GB, 256GB, 512GB), Color (Blue, Silver, Gold)
  • Variation 1: Network=AT&T, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue
  • Variation 2: Network=Unlocked, Storage=512GB, Color=Silver

Key Distinction:

  • Attributes/Aspects describe the item as a whole (e.g., Brand=Apple applies to all variations)
  • Traits describe differences between variations (e.g., Color=Blue vs Color=Silver)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Concept Level Definition Primary Use Item Listing A listing on eBay (SSKU or MSKU) Core entity for product analysis Variation SKU Specific SKU within MSKU item SKU-level inventory/pricing Product Catalog eBay Product ID (ePID) grouping Cross-listing analysis Attribute Item metadata Seller-provided properties Product filtering, classification Aspect Item metadata SAP-processed standardized properties Search indexing, recommendations Trait Variation metadata Variation-level differentiators SKU differentiation

docs.title: Purpose and scope
docs.text:
This guide explains how Core Listing Service (CLS) produces and changes the listing information used by the Item LDM. It uses a small set of canonical business events so users can understand the data without learning every endpoint or storage document. The canonical names are documentation labels; the repository event names are retained as evidence where CLS publishes them.

CLS records accepted listing state. It does not by itself decide final buyer eligibility, checkout price, search or View Item rendering, policy outcomes, delivery promises, orders, refunds, or payments. The Item LDM can also combine CLS state with catalog, classification, warehouse, search, and other downstream sources.

docs.title: Event overview
docs.text:
Canonical business event Action Business description Representative CLS evidence Listing created Produce A seller or authorized workflow submits a new listing and CLS accepts its identity, seller context, and initial listing information. Core item/listing create flows Listing revised Update A seller or authorized workflow changes listing content or configuration, such as title, category, condition, media, shipping, payment, tax, returns, or policies. ITEM.CATEGORY.UPDATED; item/listing update flows Offer or availability changed Update Price, quantity, auction terms, offers, promotions, or inventory availability changes. ITEM.AVL.UPDATED, ITEM.LOCK.EXPIRED Listing lifecycle changed Update A listing is scheduled, activated, renewed, ended, finalized, or relisted. LISTING.RENEW, LISTING.END Listing control changed Update A hold, restriction, administrative action, safety control, or privacy-related control changes the accepted state. ITEM.HOLDSTATUS.UPDATED; administrative and PII operations Listing reconciled Operational signal A migration, dual-write, repair, or consistency process asks other systems to reconcile listing state. LISTING.RECONCILE, ITEM.DUALWRITE.FAILED Listing data removed or privacy-cleared Clear/remove Supported personal information is cleared or anonymized, or a supported entity is removed. Privacy clearing is not the same as ending a listing. PII removal and deletion processors Draft changed Produce/update/remove A seller creates, revises, reconciles, or deletes working draft information. A draft is not a live listing. DRAFT.CREATE, DRAFT.UPDATE, draft dual-write failure signals Derived or exposed state Derived/expose CLS exposes current state and revision history; downstream systems may derive, standardize, or enrich additional Item LDM values. Current-state reads, revision-history reads, downstream Item LDM sources

An event is not necessarily a complete listing snapshot. Some events are facts about a state change, some tell consumers to re-read current state, and some are repair or failure signals.

docs.title: Listing created
docs.text: When a seller or authorized eBay workflow submits a listing, CLS validates and records the listing identity, marketplace and seller context, application or channel information, and initial seller-provided content. Consumers can use this event category to understand when listing state was first accepted, but creation alone does not prove that the listing is live, buyer-visible, or successfully sold.

docs.title: Listing revised
docs.text: When a seller or authorized workflow changes what is being offered or how it is presented, CLS accepts and records the revised content or configuration, including categories, condition, media, shipping, payment, tax, returns, and other listing settings. Consumers can use this category to understand the latest seller-configured listing state, while standardized or enriched values may be supplied by other processes.

docs.title: Offer or availability changed
docs.text: When an inventory or listing workflow changes price, quantity, auction or offer terms, promotions, or availability, CLS records the accepted commercial state and may publish an availability signal. Consumers should treat an availability signal as a prompt to refresh the listing state, not as a complete price or quantity snapshot; listing-currency price is not the final buyer price or checkout total.

docs.title: Listing lifecycle changed
docs.text: When a seller, scheduler, or authorized eBay operation schedules, activates, renews, ends, finalizes, or relists a listing, CLS records the resulting status, dates, duration, end reason, auction outcome, or relist relationship. Consumers can use this category to understand the lifecycle state recorded by CLS, but lifecycle state alone does not establish search visibility, purchase eligibility, checkout availability, or order outcomes.

docs.title: Listing control changed
docs.text: When eBay operations or a safety, administrative, or privacy workflow places a hold, applies a restriction, ends or reinstates a listing administratively, or changes a supported control, CLS records the resulting state. Consumers can use this category to identify controls recorded by CLS, but one control value does not represent the complete policy, fraud, visibility, or buyer-eligibility decision.

docs.title: Listing reconciled
docs.text: When migration, dual-write, repair, or consistency work detects that listing state may need correction, CLS can publish a reconciliation or failure signal for other systems. Consumers can use this category to identify operational coordination, but it should not be interpreted as a seller revision or as proof that every downstream copy has already been corrected.

docs.title: Listing data removed or privacy-cleared
docs.text: When a supported privacy or deletion operation removes personal information, CLS clears or anonymizes the supported values and may remove supported entity state. Consumers must distinguish privacy clearing from listing ending and from physical deletion; the resulting record may continue to exist with specific values removed.

docs.title: Draft changed
docs.text: When a seller saves, revises, reconciles, or deletes a draft, CLS records the seller's working state and maintains draft associations where supported. Consumers can use this category to understand saved seller work, but a draft does not prove publication, buyer visibility, or purchase eligibility.

docs.title: Derived or exposed state
docs.text: After CLS accepts a business event, consumers can retrieve the latest recorded listing state and, where supported, revision history. The Item LDM may also derive or enrich values from catalog, classification, warehouse, search, or dimensional sources. These values should be interpreted using their field definitions and source lineage rather than assumed to be direct CLS writes.

docs.title: Consumer contract
docs.text: Consumers can use the Item LDM to understand listing information accepted by CLS, the recorded commercial and lifecycle state, seller working drafts where applicable, and changes or signals that CLS records or publishes. They must combine it with other data before concluding what a buyer will pay, whether a buyer can complete checkout, how policy or fraud rules were applied, what View Item will display, how an order or payment completed, or what delivery outcome occurred.

docs.title: Source and repository boundary
docs.text:
The Item LDM documentation is broader than the CLS source model. Some fields are derived, standardized, historical, dimensional, financial, or search values from sources other than CLS. The mapping marks those fields as Derived or exposed rather than attributing them to a CLS event without evidence.

During migration between legacy and current listing paths, the same business change can reach different consumers at different times. Current state, revision history, event signals, and downstream LDM values may therefore have different availability timing.

docs.title: Scope and answer
docs.text:
This is a repository-scoped walkthrough of crlstngsv. In this document, “NuDoc” means the NuData/MonStor document classes and docsets represented by this repository. The repository does not use SQL DDL for these stores; it builds JSON documents and sends MonStor RequestFactory insert, upsert, update, and delete mutations.

There are 22 declared logical docsets in the source:

Keyspace family Domain purpose Logical docsets Count ItemKeyspace Current-state identity and operational data for one listing item or variation __ROOT__, ItemCompatibility, ItemDescription, ItemQtyPrice, ItemDetails, BusinessPolicies, UuidMap, ItemLock 8 ItemGroupKeyspace Shared current-state data for an MSKU item group __ROOT__, GroupDescription, GroupBusinessPolicies 3 ListingDraft Working content and session state before or during listing publication __ROOT__, ItemDraft, ItemGroupDraft, ItemDraftCompatibility, ItemGroupDraftCompatibility, ItemGroupDraftDesc 6 UserListingDraft User-scoped index of active listing drafts UserItemDraftMap 1 ListingRevisionKeyspace Historical listing and variation changes, separate from current state __ROOT__, ListingRevision, ListingRevisionDetail, VariationRevisionDetail 4 Total 22

For ordinary live data writes, the item create/replace family writes six docsets, item-group create/replace writes three, an SSKU draft writes two or three documents and an MSKU draft writes three plus one ItemDraft per variation, or four plus one when group compatibility is present, active user-draft indexing writes one, and a revision insert writes one to three document types. UuidMap and ItemLock are auxiliary item docsets. Archive hold/version fallback writes the root docset in an archive keyspace. Therefore, “22 tables” is the schema declaration count, not the number of documents written by every request.

If a keyspace-qualified sink is counted only when a write is proven in code, there are 24 sink pairs:

  • 8 in live ItemKeyspace;
  • 3 in live ItemGroupKeyspace;
  • 6 in ListingDraft;
  • 1 in UserListingDraft;
  • 4 in ListingRevisionKeyspace;
  • 1 archive pair, ItemKeyspaceArchive/__ROOT__;
  • 1 archive pair, ItemGroupKeyspaceArchive/__ROOT__.

The archive keyspaces reuse the item and group schema classes, so they add two physical keyspace/docset sinks but no new logical docset class. The count does not claim that all 24 sinks are touched by one business operation.

The five rows above are the logical live keyspaces described by this document. ItemKeyspaceArchive and ItemGroupKeyspaceArchive are archive variants that reuse the root schemas; they are physical write targets, not additional logical keyspace families.

docs.title: Keyspace and docset purpose catalog
docs.text: This catalog explains what each keyspace represents and why each docset exists. The hierarchy role describes the document's relationship to its ancestor; it does not imply that every docset is written by every operation.

docs.title: ItemKeyspace
docs.text:
ItemKeyspace is the current-state family for one individual listing item or one variation of an MSKU listing. The item root is the identity anchor. Compatibility, description, quantity/price, details, and business-policy payloads are separated so they can be read and updated independently. UuidMap and ItemLock are auxiliary operational trees in the same keyspace, not additional parts of the normal six-docset item create/replace payload.

Docset Description and purpose Hierarchy and key context __ROOT__ (ItemRoot) Broad current-state item document: listing identity, seller/location, lifecycle, category, policy references, flags, identifiers, media references, and other item-level state. Root of the item ancestor tree; persisted primary key PK, normally equal to itemId. ItemCompatibility Fitment and compatibility payload for the item, with expanded or compressed representation. Child of the item ancestor; ItemCompID, normally COMPAT_<itemId>. ItemDescription Seller/item description payload and its revision timestamp, with expanded or compressed representation. Child of the item ancestor; ItemDescID, normally DESC_<itemId>. ItemQtyPrice Commercial and inventory state: available quantity, sold quantity, remnant quantity, and price variants. Child of the item ancestor; ItemQtyPriceID, normally QTY_PRICE_<itemId>. ItemDetails Additional item-level details such as high-precision prices, relaxed rules, source listing, and supporting documents. Child of the item ancestor; itemDetailsID, normally ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId>. BusinessPolicies Item-level return, payment, and shipping policy content and identifiers. Child of the item ancestor; plcsId, normally BIZ_POL_<itemId>. UuidMap (ItemUUIDMapping) Auxiliary seller-and-UUID lookup that resolves listingId and listingAppId for UUID-specific operations. Separate UUID ancestor tree in the same keyspace; composite key is seller ID plus UUID, with UUID_MAP child semantics. ItemLock Inventory reservation lifecycle state for active, committed, cancelled, and extended locks, including the aggregate summary lock. Auxiliary child under the item ancestor; persisted key pk, normally LOCK_<lockId>; summary key is LOCK_$$$SUMMARY$$$.

docs.title: ItemGroupKeyspace
docs.text:
ItemGroupKeyspace stores shared current-state data for an MSKU group. It identifies group membership and variation context while keeping variation-specific price, quantity, lifecycle, and other sellable state in the individual ItemKeyspace families. The group root references member item IDs; this is a logical relationship across keyspaces, not a cross-keyspace parent-child key.

Docset Description and purpose Hierarchy and key context __ROOT__ (ItemGroupRoot) Group identity, member item IDs, shared title/images, variation traits, group identifiers, version, and group lifecycle data. Root of the group ancestor tree; persisted primary key PK, normally equal to groupId. GroupDescription Shared description for the group, optionally compressed, with its revision timestamp. Child of the group ancestor; groupDescId, normally GROUP_DESC_<groupId>. GroupBusinessPolicies Shared group-level return, payment, and shipping policy content. Child of the group ancestor; plcsId, normally BIZ_POL_<groupId>. It inherits the policy field shape but has a distinct collection.

docs.title: ListingDraft
docs.text:
ListingDraft is the working-state family used while a listing is being constructed or revised before publication. A single draftId ancestor can contain SSKU item content, MSKU group content, compatibility content, group description content, and one ItemDraft per active MSKU variation. These docsets are storage children of the same draft ancestor even when one docset is logically associated with the item or group portion.

Docset Description and purpose Hierarchy and key context __ROOT__ (ListingDraftRoot) Draft session state, flags, scratch values, progress metadata, dates, and the list of variation item IDs. Root of the draft ancestor tree; persisted primary key PK, normally equal to draftId. ItemDraft Draft content for an SSKU item or one MSKU variation, including title, description, price, quantity, seller, terms, categories, media, and revision metadata. Direct child of the draft ancestor; PK, normally ITEM_<draftId> for SSKU or ITEM_<draftId>_<variationId> for an MSKU variation. ItemDraftCompatibility Optional SSKU compatibility payload for the draft item. Direct storage child of the draft ancestor, logically associated with ItemDraft; DraftCompID, normally COMPAT_<draftId>. ItemGroupDraft Shared MSKU draft-group content: group title, images, variation traits, seller group key, policies, and group ID. Direct child of the draft ancestor; PK, normally GROUP_<draftId>. ItemGroupDraftDesc Optional shared MSKU group description and description revision metadata. Direct storage child of the draft ancestor, logically associated with ItemGroupDraft; PK, normally GROUPDESC_<draftId>. ItemGroupDraftCompatibility Optional MSKU group-level compatibility payload. Direct storage child of the draft ancestor, logically associated with ItemGroupDraft; DraftCompID, normally GROUPCOMPAT_<draftId>.

docs.title: UserListingDraft
docs.text:
UserListingDraft is an index family for finding active listing drafts by user. It stores summary and lookup metadata rather than the full draft payload. It is intentionally separate from ListingDraft, so a user-index mutation does not automatically mutate the draft content tree.

Docset Description and purpose Hierarchy and key context UserItemDraftMap (UserListingDraftMap) User-scoped summary of an active draft, including draftId, user, title, marketplace/application, category, images, creation mode, and timestamps. User-and-draft composite ancestor key; the schema class has no persisted primary-key field. Conceptually UserListingDraft/<userId>/<draftId>.

docs.title: ListingRevisionKeyspace
docs.text:
ListingRevisionKeyspace stores historical changes rather than the latest listing state. A listing ancestor can have an optional retention root, one or more generated revision documents, and detail children describing the non-variation and variation properties changed by each revision.

Docset Description and purpose Hierarchy and key context __ROOT__ (ListingRevisionRoot) Conditional retention state for a listing's revision history, including the listing identifier and TTL-maintenance fields. Optional sibling under the listing ancestor; lstgId identifies the listing. Normal revision inserts do not create it. ListingRevision Revision summary: changed property groups, revision/version identifiers, application, significant revision count, creation flag, and revision timestamp. Generated child of the listing ancestor; the schema has no persisted key field. ListingRevisionDetail Non-variation property-level change record with property group, property, change type, old value, new value, and display label. Generated child of a particular ListingRevision; the schema has no persisted key field. VariationRevisionDetail Variation-specific property-level change record with variation ID, changed variation property, trait values, change type, and old/new values. Generated child of a particular ListingRevision; the schema has no persisted key field.

docs.title: 1. End-to-end producer flow
docs.text:
The common path is:

REST resource or V1 dual-write trigger
  -> validation and processor selection
  -> V2 model-to-NuData document converter
  -> ancestor/child key construction
  -> transactional MonStor mutation
  -> later multi-docset get/query response

The V2 resources call processors directly. V1 listing and draft resources first pass through DualWriteProcessor or DraftDualWriteProcessor; those processors convert legacy payloads to V2 models and decide whether the NuData write is asynchronous, synchronous, parallel, or disabled by a ramp/config gate. A successful V2 write is not evidence that Oracle/Caty was or was not also written; those systems are outside this document's count.

The persistence boundary is a set of documents under an item, group, draft, user, or listing-revision ancestor. DocumentConverter, ItemGroupDocumentConverter, and DraftDocumentConverter construct the content. The processors then use MonStor InsertRequest, BatchMutateRequest, UpdateRequest, or DeleteRequest, generally with transactional options for multi-document operations. Consumers read current item and group state with multi-docset gets, read drafts through draft queries/gets, read active drafts through UserItemDraftMap, and read revision history through ancestor queries.

docs.title: 1.1. From request input to Java entity
docs.text:
There are two main producer entry paths:

  1. Direct V2 client input. A caller sends a JSON request to a V2 resource. The web framework binds the request body to the Java parameter declared by the resource: Item, ItemGroup, PriceAndQuantity, ListingDraft, or another operation-specific request type. The resource performs authorization and passes that typed object to the corresponding processor. For example, CoreItemResource.createItem(Item) passes an Item to CoreItemProcessor.insertItem(Item, ...), while CoreItemGroupResource.createItemGroup(ItemGroup) passes an ItemGroup to CoreItemGroupProcessor.insertItemGroup(ItemGroup, ...).

  2. Legacy V1 dual-write input. A legacy listing request is first represented by V1 Java entities such as Listing, ListingDetails, and SaleBo. DualWriteProcessor invokes ListingConverter, which builds one or more V2 Item objects and, only for an MSKU listing, an ItemGroup. The V1 listing ID, variation data, seller SKU, pricing, quantity, lifecycle, policies, and other source values are normalized into the V2 model before any NuData document is built. Runtime ramps can make this conversion/write synchronous, asynchronous, parallel, or disabled.

The important boundary is that NuData writers do not normally serialize the incoming HTTP JSON directly into storage. The request is first represented as a Java domain/request object, then passed through the processor and converter logic that applies the path's validation and normalization. The Java object is the source of truth for the document-building step described below.

docs.title: 1.2. Item producer path
docs.text:
For a direct V2 item create or replace, the flow is:

JSON request body
  -> Java Item
  -> CoreItemProcessor.insertItem/upsertItem
  -> DocumentConverter
  -> six ItemKeyspace Documents
  -> ancestor/child Keys
  -> transactional MonStor InsertRequest

CoreItemProcessor derives stable child identifiers from itemId, such as COMPAT_<itemId>, DESC_<itemId>, QTY_PRICE_<itemId>, ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId>, and BIZ_POL_<itemId>. It then asks DocumentConverter to build:

Java source object Converter method NuData document Item getRoot(item) ItemKeyspace/__ROOT__ Item getItemCompatibility(item, compatibilityId) ItemKeyspace/ItemCompatibility Item getDescription(item, descriptionId) ItemKeyspace/ItemDescription Item getQtyPrice(item, qtyPriceId) ItemKeyspace/ItemQtyPrice Item getItemDetails(item, itemDetailsId) ItemKeyspace/ItemDetails Item.businessPolicies getBusinessPolicies(..., bizPolId) ItemKeyspace/BusinessPolicies

Each converter creates a NuData schema object, copies or transforms Java properties, serializes that object through the configured Jackson ObjectMapper into an ObjectNode, and wraps it with DocumentFactory.createDocument(...). Examples of transformations include category and lifecycle construction, image conversion, amount conversion, expanded-versus-compressed descriptions and compatibilities, and conversion of return/payment/shipping terms.

The processor then builds the item ancestor key and child keys, adds the six documents to a transactional MonStor request, and executes it. A create path uses addForInsert; a replace/upsert path uses addForUpsert and can apply a core-listing-version filter to prevent an older update from overwriting newer state. A successful response means the accepted current item state has been written to the six logical docsets; it does not mean every possible auxiliary docset such as UuidMap or ItemLock was written.

docs.title: 1.3. ItemGroup producer path
docs.text:
For a direct V2 item-group create or the processor's upsert path, the flow is:

JSON request body
  -> Java ItemGroup
  -> CoreItemGroupProcessor.insertItemGroup/upsertItemGroup
  -> ItemGroupDocumentConverter + DocumentConverter
  -> three ItemGroupKeyspace Documents
  -> ancestor/child Keys
  -> transactional MonStor InsertRequest

CoreItemGroupProcessor derives GROUP_DESC_<groupId> and BIZ_POL_<groupId>, then builds:

Java source object Converter method NuData document ItemGroup ItemGroupDocumentConverter.getRoot(group, lastModifiedDate) ItemGroupKeyspace/__ROOT__ ItemGroup ItemGroupDocumentConverter.getDescription(group, descriptionId) ItemGroupKeyspace/GroupDescription ItemGroup.businessPolicies DocumentConverter.getBusinessPolicies(..., bizPolId) ItemGroupKeyspace/GroupBusinessPolicies

The group root contains group identity, member variation IDs, shared images, variation traits, group version, and group-level identifiers. The description and policy documents are separate child documents so they can be updated independently. The group processor adds all three documents to one transactional request; it does not write variation price or quantity into the group root.

The current CoreItemGroupResource replace methods are stubs that return null; the processor upsert path is nevertheless used by the V1 dual-write flow and is the code-proven group replacement implementation described here.

docs.title: 1.4. SSKU/MSKU conversion and write branching
docs.text:
The legacy conversion path determines whether a group exists before the NuData write:

V1 Listing + SaleBo
  -> ListingConverter.getItemsFromListing(...)
       -> one Item for SSKU
       -> one Item per active variation for MSKU
  -> ListingConverter.getItemGroupFromListing(...)
       -> null for SSKU
       -> one ItemGroup for MSKU
  -> group write (MSKU only)
  -> item write or batch item write

For an MSKU listing, ListingConverter creates the group ID from the parent listing ID, collects the active variation item IDs into ItemGroup.itemIds, and assigns that parent ID to each variation Item.groupId. Shared description, business policies, compatibilities, and some identifiers are stored on the group and cleared from the variation Item objects instead of being repeated. CoreItemProcessor.insertItems(...) then builds and inserts the complete six-document item family for each variation.

For an SSKU listing, the converter returns one ordinary Item and no ItemGroup; the processor writes only the item family. An MSKU with one active variation still takes the MSKU branch and writes an ItemGroup whose itemIds contains one variation ID.

docs.title: 1.5. Draft input follows the same boundary with a draft model
docs.text: For V2 listing drafts, the request body is bound to ListingDraft. The draft processor validates it and DraftDocumentConverter builds the draft root, item drafts, optional group draft, descriptions, and compatibility documents. The converter assigns or normalizes draft variation IDs, serializes each NuData schema object into a Document, and the processor writes the assembled documents transactionally. SSKU drafts have item content without a group draft; MSKU drafts have group content plus one item draft per variation.

docs.title: 1.6. Partial updates do not rebuild the whole Java entity
docs.text: Operation-specific requests such as price/quantity, category, product reference, hold status, business-policy reference, description, or item lock updates can bypass the full create/replace conversion. The processor converts only the changed request data or builds an update operation directly against the affected root or child docset. For example, price/quantity changes target ItemQtyPrice and related root state, a category change targets the root category fields, and a lock operation writes ItemLock plus its inventory side effect. Therefore, “one item write” may mean a six-docset replacement or a narrower mutation of one or two existing docsets.

docs.title: 2. Schema, key layout, field inventory, and model lineage
docs.text: Docset is the repository's schema abstraction: a Java class represents a NuData collection and getCollectionName() returns the collection name (crlstngsvService/src/main/java/com/ebay/app/cls/nudata/Docset.java). Nested helper classes such as Price, Lifecycle, TermsAndPolicies, and ShippingTerms are fields inside a document; they are not separate docsets.

docs.title: Item family: ItemKeyspace
docs.text:
The root key is KeyFactory.create(itemId). The child documents are descendants of that root:

itemId
├── ItemCompatibility / COMPAT_<itemId>
├── ItemDescription / DESC_<itemId>
├── ItemQtyPrice / QTY_PRICE_<itemId>
├── BusinessPolicies / BIZ_POL_<itemId>
├── ItemDetails / ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId>
└── ItemLock / LOCK_<lockId>

The lock-summary document uses the same ItemLock schema and reserved identifier LOCK_$$$SUMMARY$$$. Lock mutations also update ItemQtyPrice to reflect reserved inventory. UuidMap uses a different key shape: UUID_<sellerId>/<uuid> with a UUID_MAP child.

Docset Document role and representative fields __ROOT__ Core listing state: PK, title, category, lifecycle, seller/listing identifiers, location, images, policies/terms references, version/revision fields, onHold, endRsn, and other item-level state. DocumentConverter.getRoot() maps the V2 Item into this document. ItemCompatibility Fitment/compatibility payload: ItemCompID, compat or compressed cmpCompat, and ftExempt. ItemDescription Description payload: ItemDescID, desc or compressed compDesc, and descRevsnDt. ItemQtyPrice Inventory and commercial values: availQty, qtySold, price, and minRmntSet; price contains fixed, auction, marketing, original-retail, cost-of-goods, and price-guarantee data. ItemDetails Additional item details such as hasRlxdRls, high-precision fixed/start prices, source listing, and supporting documents. BusinessPolicies Policy content: policy identifiers plus return, payment, and shipping terms. UuidMap UUID/seller lookup value containing listingId and listingAppId; used to resolve or anonymize a listing mapping. ItemLock Reservation/lock documents with pk, status (A, C, X), quantity, expiration, timestamps, and UUID; the summary record stores aggregate reserved quantity.

The six-document item create/replace set is: __ROOT__, ItemCompatibility, ItemDescription, ItemQtyPrice, ItemDetails, and BusinessPolicies. The UuidMap and ItemLock documents are not part of the normal item payload mutation.

docs.title: ItemKeyspace elaboration
docs.text: ItemKeyspace is the current-state store for one individual listing item. __ROOT__ holds the broad item state, while the child docsets isolate compatibility, description, quantity/price, details, and business-policy content that can be updated independently. UuidMap and ItemLock support lookup and reservation workflows rather than representing additional top-level item payloads. Consumers should use the item root as the identity anchor and treat child documents as parts of the same item state, not as independent listings.

docs.title: Relationship between ItemKeyspace and ItemGroupKeyspace
docs.text:
These are separate keyspace families with separate ancestors and separate root documents. ItemKeyspace stores the individual item or variation records; ItemGroupKeyspace stores the multi-variation group identity, membership, shared traits, group description, and group-level policies. For an MSKU group, the group root's itemIds identifies its member item roots, and the item root's grpId points back to the group. This is a logical relationship, not a parent-child key relationship across keyspaces.

The two families therefore have different write responsibilities: item operations write variation/listing state such as quantity, price, lifecycle, description, and item compatibility, while group operations write membership, variation traits, group description, and group policies. A consumer must read both families to reconstruct a complete MSKU listing; a group document alone does not contain the full variation-level commercial state, and an item document alone does not establish the complete group membership.

docs.title: Single-SKU versus one-variation MSKU
docs.text:
The repository distinguishes SSKU versus MSKU by the listing's MSKU flag, not by counting variation records:

Listing condition ItemKeyspace result ItemGroupKeyspace result SSKU (saleBo.isMsku() is false) One ordinary item document family is created or updated. No ItemGroup record is created; getItemGroupFromListing(...) returns null. MSKU with one active/non-deleted variation One item record is created for that variation. Its groupId points to the parent listing/group ID. The MSKU group is still created with __ROOT__, GroupDescription, and GroupBusinessPolicies; the group root's itemIds contains exactly that one variation item ID. MSKU with multiple active/non-deleted variations One item record is created per active variation. The same group docsets are created, and itemIds contains all active variation item IDs.

For the one-variation MSKU case, the group record is therefore not omitted or collapsed into the item record. The group ID is the parent listing ID, while the sole itemIds value is the separate variation item ID. A consumer should not infer “SSKU” merely because itemIds has length one; it must use the listing's MSKU classification and the presence of the group record.

docs.title: Item-group family: ItemGroupKeyspace
docs.text:
The group root is KeyFactory.create(groupId). Child keys are descendants:

groupId
├── GroupDescription / GROUP_DESC_<groupId>
└── GroupBusinessPolicies / BIZ_POL_<groupId>
Docset Document role and representative fields __ROOT__ Group identity and membership: PK, title, itemIds, seller/group key, variation traits, images, group version, group draft ID, and administrative/lifecycle fields. GroupDescription Group description, optionally compressed, with groupDescId and grpDescRevsnDt. GroupBusinessPolicies Group-level business policies. It extends the business-policy model but returns the group-specific collection name.

CoreItemGroupProcessor creates or upserts all three documents transactionally. Group shipping updates touch the root and GroupBusinessPolicies; description updates touch the root and GroupDescription.

docs.title: ItemGroupKeyspace elaboration
docs.text: ItemGroupKeyspace is the current-state store for an item group, most notably the shared structure of an MSKU listing. Its root describes the group and its member IDs; GroupDescription and GroupBusinessPolicies hold independently addressable group content. GroupBusinessPolicies uses the group collection name even though its fields inherit the item policy schema, so it must not be counted as the item BusinessPolicies docset. Group-level state also does not replace the item-level documents for the group's variations.

docs.title: Listing-draft family: ListingDraft
docs.text:
The draft root is keyed by draftId. The processor uses prefixes such as GROUP_, GROUPDESC_, GROUPCOMPAT_, ITEM_, and COMPAT_. The key relationship is:

draftId
├── ItemDraft / ITEM_<draftId>                 (SSKU)
├── ItemDraftCompatibility / COMPAT_<draftId>  (optional SSKU)
├── ItemGroupDraft / GROUP_<draftId>            (MSKU)
├── ItemGroupDraftDesc / GROUPDESC_<draftId>   (MSKU)
├── ItemGroupDraftCompatibility / GROUPCOMPAT_<draftId> (optional MSKU)
└── ItemDraft / ITEM_<draftId>_<variationId>   (MSKU variations)
Docset Document role and representative fields __ROOT__ Draft session, flags, scratch details, draft/creation/revision dates, and the list of MSKU variation IDs. ItemDraft SSKU or variation content including title, description, price, quantity, seller, listing terms, categories, images, and revision fields. ItemGroupDraft MSKU group title, images, variation traits, seller group key, business policies, and group ID. ItemDraftCompatibility Optional SSKU compatibility payload, compressed when configured. ItemGroupDraftCompatibility Optional MSKU group compatibility payload, compressed when configured. ItemGroupDraftDesc MSKU group description, optionally compressed, plus description revision date.

An SSKU draft normally writes two or three docsets: root, item, and optional item compatibility. An MSKU draft writes root, group, group description, optional group compatibility, and one or more ItemDraft variation documents. The variation count changes the number of documents, not the number of logical docsets.

docs.title: ListingDraft elaboration
docs.text: ListingDraft is a working-state store for listing construction before or during publication. SSKU drafts use item documents, while MSKU drafts add a group root, group description, optional group compatibility, and one item document per variation. Draft documents are not proof that a live ItemKeyspace or ItemGroupKeyspace listing exists; they are a separate content model and lifecycle.

docs.title: User active-draft family: UserListingDraft
docs.text: UserItemDraftMap is keyed below a user root and draft identifier. Its representative fields are draftId, marketplace/application identifiers, category, title, image URLs, creation mode/date, user ID, and lastModifiedDate. It is a separate index/map from the content in ListingDraft; updating or deleting one does not imply that the other is automatically changed unless the caller invokes both flows.

docs.title: UserListingDraft elaboration
docs.text: UserListingDraft is an index for finding active drafts by user. Its UserItemDraftMap document contains summary metadata and lookup identifiers, not the complete draft payload. It can therefore be created, updated, or deleted independently of the corresponding ListingDraft content, subject to the caller's dual-write behavior.

docs.title: Revision-history family: ListingRevisionKeyspace
docs.text:
The listing ID is the ancestor. A normal insert creates a generated child key for ListingRevision, then generated child keys for optional details:

listingId
├── __ROOT__ / listingId [optional TTL-maintenance root]
└── ListingRevision / generated-guid
    ├── ListingRevisionDetail / generated-guid (zero or more)
    └── VariationRevisionDetail / generated-guid (zero or more)

The __ROOT__ document is an optional sibling under the listing ancestor. It is created or updated by expired-date maintenance, not by the normal revision insert. ListingRevision contains revised property groups, version/application identifiers, significant revision count, revised date, and updated core-listing version. Detail documents contain revised group/property, change type, old/new values, and (for variation details) variation traits/ID.

The declared revision root class exists as a schema class and is queried by the revision-history code, but RevisionHistoryNudataClient.addForInsert() explicitly does not create a root document in the normal insert path. A separate expired-date upsert path can create/update that root, so it remains a declared and conditional write target rather than a normal revision-insert target.

docs.title: ListingRevisionKeyspace elaboration
docs.text: ListingRevisionKeyspace is historical rather than current-state storage. ListingRevision records a revision summary under a listing ancestor, and detail children record property-level changes, including variation-specific changes. A revision document should be interpreted as an event/history record, not as a replacement for the latest ItemKeyspace or ItemGroupKeyspace state. The declared revision root is an exception: it participates in expired-date maintenance but is intentionally omitted from ordinary revision inserts.

docs.title: Detailed field schema and source-model lineage
docs.text: The following inventory lists the JSON properties declared directly on each docset class. Java types are included where they clarify whether a field is a scalar, list, enum, or embedded object. Fields inside embedded objects are not repeated as docsets: for example, ItemKeyspace/__ROOT__.category is a Category value containing category fields, but Category is not another NuData collection. The source classes use Jackson annotations, so the JSON property names below are the persisted names, not necessarily the Java member names. For item and item-group docsets, each table also includes the write-side source property or expression.

docs.title: Complete NuDoc hierarchies and primary keys
docs.text: NuData uses several independent ancestor trees. A keyspace is a storage namespace that can contain more than one tree; ItemKeyspace, for example, contains the normal item tree, the UUID lookup tree, and the item-lock subtree. A docset is a child of another docset only when its storage key is constructed beneath that ancestor. Sharing a keyspace does not by itself make two docsets parent and child.

docs.title: Item current-state and auxiliary lookup trees
docs.text:
ItemKeyspace
├── itemId [ItemRoot / PK]
│   ├── ItemCompatibility / COMPAT_<itemId> [ItemCompID]
│   ├── ItemDescription / DESC_<itemId> [ItemDescID]
│   ├── ItemQtyPrice / QTY_PRICE_<itemId> [ItemQtyPriceID]
│   ├── ItemDetails / ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId> [itemDetailsID]
│   ├── BusinessPolicies / BIZ_POL_<itemId> [plcsId]
│   └── ItemLock / LOCK_<lockId> [pk; summary: LOCK_$$$SUMMARY$$$]
└── UUID_<sellerId>/<uuid>
    └── UuidMap / UUID_MAP [seller ID + UUID]

UuidMap is an auxiliary lookup tree, not a child payload of ItemRoot. ItemLock uses the item ancestor and is operationally associated with the quantity/price document because lock mutations update reserved inventory there as a side effect.

docs.title: Item-group current-state tree
docs.text:
ItemGroupKeyspace
└── groupId [ItemGroupRoot / PK]
    ├── GroupDescription / GROUP_DESC_<groupId> [groupDescId]
    └── GroupBusinessPolicies / BIZ_POL_<groupId> [plcsId]

docs.title: Listing-draft tree
docs.text:
ListingDraft
└── draftId [ListingDraftRoot / PK]
    ├── ItemDraft / ITEM_<draftId> [PK]                         (SSKU)
    ├── ItemDraftCompatibility / COMPAT_<draftId> [DraftCompID] (optional SSKU)
    ├── ItemGroupDraft / GROUP_<draftId> [PK]                  (MSKU)
    ├── ItemGroupDraftDesc / GROUPDESC_<draftId> [PK]          (MSKU)
    ├── ItemGroupDraftCompatibility / GROUPCOMPAT_<draftId> [DraftCompID] (optional MSKU)
    └── ItemDraft / ITEM_<draftId>_<variationId> [PK]           (MSKU variation)

All six logical docsets are storage children of the same draftId ancestor. The compatibility and group-description documents are logically associated with the item or group portion of the draft, but they are not nested beneath those documents in the storage key path. An MSKU draft can contain multiple ItemDraft documents, one for each active variation.

docs.title: Active-user draft index tree
docs.text:
UserListingDraft
└── userId
    └── UserItemDraftMap / draftId [composite key: userId + draftId]

UserItemDraftMap has no persisted key field in its schema class; its key is the composite user-and-draft ancestor shape. The repository documents the two-part key but does not expose a serialized delimiter or additional prefix. It is separate from the full ListingDraft content tree.

docs.title: Listing-revision history tree
docs.text:
ListingRevisionKeyspace
└── listingId [revision ancestor]
    ├── __ROOT__ / listingId [lstgId; optional TTL-maintenance root]
    └── ListingRevision / <generated-guid> [no persisted key field]
        ├── ListingRevisionDetail / <generated-guid> [no persisted key field]
        └── VariationRevisionDetail / <generated-guid> [no persisted key field]

The revision root is conditional: TTL maintenance can upsert it, but the normal revision-insert path starts at ListingRevision. Detail documents are children of a particular generated revision key.

docs.title: Primary-key and key-shape inventory
docs.text:
Hierarchy Docset Primary key / key shape Representative storage key Item current-state __ROOT__ PK itemId Item current-state ItemCompatibility ItemCompID COMPAT_<itemId> Item current-state ItemDescription ItemDescID DESC_<itemId> Item current-state ItemQtyPrice ItemQtyPriceID QTY_PRICE_<itemId> Item current-state ItemDetails itemDetailsID ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId> Item current-state BusinessPolicies plcsId BIZ_POL_<itemId> Item lock subtree ItemLock pk LOCK_<lockId>; summary LOCK_$$$SUMMARY$$$ UUID lookup UuidMap Seller ID and UUID UUID_<sellerId>/<uuid> with UUID_MAP child Item-group current-state __ROOT__ PK groupId Item-group current-state GroupDescription groupDescId GROUP_DESC_<groupId> Item-group current-state GroupBusinessPolicies plcsId BIZ_POL_<groupId> Listing draft __ROOT__ PK draftId Listing draft ItemDraft PK ITEM_<draftId> or ITEM_<draftId>_<variationId> Listing draft ItemDraftCompatibility DraftCompID COMPAT_<draftId> Listing draft ItemGroupDraft PK GROUP_<draftId> Listing draft ItemGroupDraftDesc PK GROUPDESC_<draftId> Listing draft ItemGroupDraftCompatibility DraftCompID GROUPCOMPAT_<draftId> Active-user draft index UserItemDraftMap Composite ancestor key: userId + draftId; no persisted key field UserListingDraft/<userId>/<draftId> (conceptual) Revision history __ROOT__ lstgId ancestor key listingId Revision history ListingRevision Generated child key; no persisted key field <generated-guid> under listingId Revision history ListingRevisionDetail Generated child key; no persisted key field <generated-guid> under a revision Revision history VariationRevisionDetail Generated child key; no persisted key field <generated-guid> under a revision

Archive processors reuse the item and group root schemas under ItemKeyspaceArchive and ItemGroupKeyspaceArchive. Those archive roots are additional physical sinks, not new logical docsets or new hierarchy types.

docs.title: ItemKeyspace/__ROOT__
docs.text:
The item root is the broadest item document. It combines listing identity, seller/location, lifecycle, category, policy references, flags, and item features.

docs.title: Field-schema interpretation
docs.text:
• The lists above are top-level persisted properties from the repository's Java schema classes. They are not a promise that every property is present on every document; converters may omit null values, and update paths may set or unset only a subset.
  • compat/cmpCompat and desc/compDesc show the repository's expanded versus compressed representation choice.
  • BusinessPolicies is reused by item, group, and draft models as an embedded object, while GroupBusinessPolicies is the separate group docset that inherits the same four top-level policy fields.
  • The four classes named __ROOT__ are different schemas in different packages. Their matching class names do not make them one shared collection across keyspaces.
  • getCollectionName() is the authoritative logical collection name in the source. The revision classes return their fully qualified Java class name, while the revision constants and mutation code use the short docset names ListingRevision, ListingRevisionDetail, and VariationRevisionDetail.

docs.title: Write-side lineage notes
docs.text:
The mappings in these tables follow the write-side converters, not just matching names by convention. A derived mapping means the JSON field is assembled from multiple model properties or converted to a NuData-specific embedded type. An update-only mapping is not populated by the standard create/replace converter; it is changed by a separate processor mutation.

The item root also has direct update methods that bypass full model conversion. For example, category updates set the nested category fields, price/quantity updates set selected root and child fields, and media updates set images/prdGallryFallbckURL-related root state. Therefore, the tables describe the full-document source model while partial operations may update only a subset.

The group root and child documents also have partial update paths that can change selected fields without reconstructing the entire ItemGroup payload.

docs.title: 3. Operation-to-docset write matrix
docs.text:
The matrix describes docset families, not individual documents. “Optional” means the request shape or operation determines whether the mutation is included.

Business operation NuData mutation and docsets Create/replace V2 item Insert or upsert six item docsets: __ROOT__, ItemCompatibility, ItemDescription, ItemQtyPrice, ItemDetails, BusinessPolicies. Reconcile variants can omit ItemDetails or gate compatibility updates. Bulk replace items Calls the same item upsert path independently/asynchronously per item, so the same six-docset family is possible for each item. Item compatibility update Upsert ItemCompatibility only. Item description/revision update Update item __ROOT__ revision/version fields and ItemDescription. Item price/quantity/inventory update Update ItemQtyPrice and usually __ROOT__; may also update BusinessPolicies for payment fields and upsert ItemDetails for high-precision/detail state. Quantity/lifecycle inventory update Update ItemQtyPrice and __ROOT__ for quantities, scheduled/end dates, end reason, and core-listing version. Shipping/policy update Update item __ROOT__ and BusinessPolicies; group equivalent updates touch group __ROOT__ and GroupBusinessPolicies. Category/media/version/administrative item update Usually update item __ROOT__; category, media, hold, duplicate, relist, HTTPS, and related fields are root fields. MSKU variants use batch root updates. Item lock create/reactivate/commit/cancel/extend Write/update/delete ItemLock, plus update the item ItemQtyPrice quantities and the ItemLock summary. A lock operation therefore can touch two logical docsets, with ItemQtyPrice as the inventory side effect. UUID mapping create/delete/anonymize Insert/delete UuidMap. PII deletion anonymizes the UUID mapping and clears supported PII fields in item root/business-policy documents. Delete item variations Delete item root, compatibility, description, quantity/price, business-policy, details, and lock-summary keys. Individual lock children are handled by lock lifecycle operations; this delete list is not a blanket delete of every descendant. Create/replace item group Insert or upsert group __ROOT__, GroupDescription, and GroupBusinessPolicies. Delete item group Delete group __ROOT__, GroupDescription, and GroupBusinessPolicies. Create SSKU listing draft Insert root and ItemDraft; insert ItemDraftCompatibility only when compatibility exists. Create MSKU listing draft Insert root, ItemGroupDraft, ItemGroupDraftDesc, optional ItemGroupDraftCompatibility, and one ItemDraft per variation. Update listing draft Batch upsert root and current item documents, delete removed variation items, upsert/delete the applicable compatibility docset, and upsert/delete group/group-description documents as the draft changes between MSKU and SSKU. Delete listing draft Delete root, group/group-description/group-compatibility, item compatibility, and all descendant ItemDraft documents found by ancestor query. Create/update active user draft Insert, update, or upsert one UserItemDraftMap document. Delete active user drafts Delete the selected UserItemDraftMap documents. Insert revision history Insert one ListingRevision plus zero or more ListingRevisionDetail and VariationRevisionDetail children. Bulk backfill uses the same three docsets in one accumulated request. Revision expired-date maintenance Upsert the revision-history __ROOT__ document when that maintenance path is invoked. Archive hold update ArchiveItemProcessor inherits item update logic but overrides the hold-update keyspace; the proven archive write is ItemKeyspaceArchive/__ROOT__. Archive group version update ArchiveItemGroupProcessor overrides the group-version keyspace; the proven archive write is ItemGroupKeyspaceArchive/__ROOT__.

docs.title: 4. V1 dual-write and feature-gated behavior
docs.text:
V1 listing operations do not have a second, independent NuData schema. They flow through DualWriteProcessor, which dispatches operations such as add, relist, revise inventory, end, finalize, description, shipping, media, markdown-sale, second-chance, hold, and HTTPS updates to the V2 item/group processors. The resulting docsets are therefore the same item and group families described above.

DraftDualWriteProcessor similarly converts V1 drafts into V2 ListingDraft content and can maintain the active UserItemDraftMap index. These writes may be asynchronous fire-and-forget tasks, and reconciliation or failure events can cause retries or alternate paths.

Whether a V1 request writes NuData depends on runtime configuration and ramps. The code contains controls for disabling NuData, V2-primary migration, parallel update, create/update/end dual-write, and draft dual-write behavior. Consequently, the matrix describes code-proven targets, not a guarantee that every production request reaches every target.

docs.title: Counts
docs.text: Count type Result Meaning Declared logical docsets 22 Distinct docset classes/collection names represented in the live schema packages. Nested Java value objects are excluded. Normal item create/replace targets 6 The six item documents built by CoreItemProcessor for the standard payload path. Normal item-group create/replace targets 3 Group root, group description, and group business policies. Listing-draft logical targets 6 Six declared draft docsets; one SSKU request writes root plus item and optional compatibility (2–3 documents), while an MSKU request writes root, group, description, optional compatibility, and one item document per variation (3+N or 4+N documents). User active-draft target 1 UserItemDraftMap. Normal revision insert targets 1–3 Revision plus optional listing and variation detail children; the revision root is not in this normal insert. Proven keyspace-qualified write sinks 24 The 22 live logical pairs plus two archive root pairs.

docs.title: Important boundaries
docs.text:
• The counts are for NuData/MonStor structures visible in this repository. They exclude Oracle, Caty, SaleBO, and any downstream physical stores.
  • A docset count is not a row/document count. MSKU drafts and revisions can create many documents in one logical docset.
  • A class in the package is not proof that every path writes it. For example, revision __ROOT__ is declared and read but omitted from the ordinary revision insert; UuidMap and ItemLock are auxiliary flows.
  • Archive processors mostly read archive keyspaces. Only the overridden hold and group-version methods prove archive writes in this repository.
  • Deletes are key-specific. A delete request may remove a known set of child keys and may use an ancestor query for variation documents; it should not be interpreted as a schema drop or a physical table drop.
  • The document classes expose JSON property names, but this repository does not show a complete MonStor index/partition/replication DDL. The inventory therefore describes document shape and key ancestry, not every physical storage-engine index.
  • Dual-write order, async execution, retry, rollback, and ramps affect when a write is observed and whether it is attempted. They do not create additional logical NuData docsets.

docs.title: 6. Q&A for Item and ItemGroup readers
docs.text: This section answers questions a reader familiar with eBay shopping concepts may ask when first encountering the Java entities and NuData docsets. The answers are limited to behavior shown by this repository.

docs.title: What is an Item in this service?
docs.text: Item is the Java V2 entity for one listing-level or variation-level sellable record. For an SSKU listing, it represents the single sellable item. For an MSKU listing, the service creates one Item for each active variation, with variation-specific quantity, price, identifiers, and other item state.

docs.title: What is an ItemGroup?
docs.text: ItemGroup is the Java V2 entity for the shared parent of an MSKU listing. It stores the group identity, title, membership, variation traits, shared images, group description, and group-level business policies. It is not a second copy of every variation's commercial state.

docs.title: Does every Item have an ItemGroup?
docs.text: No. An SSKU item has an ItemKeyspace record family and no corresponding ItemGroupKeyspace record. An MSKU item has an ItemGroupKeyspace group, and its item root contains grpId pointing to that group.

docs.title: If an MSKU has only one active variation, is the ItemGroup still created?
docs.text: Yes. The repository uses the MSKU classification flag, not the number of active variations, to decide whether a group exists. An MSKU with one active variation has one item record and an item-group root whose itemIds list contains exactly that one variation item ID.

docs.title: Is a one-item itemIds list evidence that the listing is SSKU?
docs.text: No. A one-entry itemIds list can be a valid one-variation MSKU group. To classify the listing, use the MSKU/SSKU behavior and the presence of the ItemGroupKeyspace group, not the list length alone.

docs.title: Is the eBay seller SKU the same as the NuData item ID?
docs.text: No. The NuData item ID (Item.itemId, persisted as PK) identifies the service record. The seller-provided SKU is represented separately by Item.sellerItemKey and persisted as slrItemKey. For a group, the seller's group key is stored on ItemGroup.sellerGroupKey.

docs.title: Does one Java Item object map to one NuData document?
docs.text: No. The Java Item is converted into an item document family. The root ItemKeyspace/__ROOT__ contains broad item state, while child docsets hold compatibility, description, quantity/price, details, and business-policy state. A full create/replace can therefore write six item docsets for one Java Item.

docs.title: Does one Java ItemGroup object map to one NuData document?
docs.text: No. A full group write creates or upserts three documents under the group ancestor: __ROOT__, GroupDescription, and GroupBusinessPolicies. ItemGroup is the source entity; the docsets are the persistence representation.

docs.title: Are ItemKeyspace and ItemGroupKeyspace SQL tables?
docs.text: They are logical NuData/MonStor keyspace families, not SQL tables shown by this repository. Each docset class defines a persisted document shape and each ancestor/child key defines where that document belongs. The counts in this document are logical docset and proven sink counts, not relational table DDL counts.

docs.title: Which fields belong to the item and which belong to the group?
docs.text: Variation-specific commercial state belongs to Item, especially quantity and price in ItemQtyPrice, along with variation identifiers and lifecycle state. Shared MSKU state belongs to ItemGroup, including membership, variation traits, group description, shared images, and group policies. The converter explicitly clears description, business policies, compatibilities, and global identifiers from MSKU variation Item objects when those values are stored at group level.

docs.title: Where is the description stored for SSKU versus MSKU?
docs.text: For SSKU, the description is written to the item's ItemDescription docset. For MSKU, the shared description is written to the group's GroupDescription docset rather than repeated on every variation item.

docs.title: Where are business policies stored for SSKU versus MSKU?
docs.text: For SSKU, return, payment, and shipping terms are written to the item's BusinessPolicies docset and related root policy fields. For MSKU, the shared terms are written to GroupBusinessPolicies; the group collection name is different even though the policy field schema is inherited from the item business-policy model.

docs.title: Where are price and quantity stored?
docs.text: Price and quantity are variation/item-level state. They are primarily written to ItemQtyPrice, whose price object contains fixed, auction, marketing, original-retail, cost-of-goods, and price-guarantee values, while availQty, qtySold, and minRmntSet hold inventory-related values. They are not represented by the group root merely because the item belongs to an MSKU group.

docs.title: Are Price, Lifecycle, and BusinessPolicies separate docsets?
docs.text: No. In the item root, Price and Lifecycle are embedded Java value objects. The policy terms inside the item root are also embedded. BusinessPolicies is a separate docset only when referring to the item policy document; the group equivalent is the separate GroupBusinessPolicies docset.

docs.title: Why do several keyspaces have a __ROOT__ class?
docs.text: The class name is reused across different Java packages, but the schemas and collections are different. ItemKeyspace/__ROOT__ is an item root, ItemGroupKeyspace/__ROOT__ is a group root, and the draft and revision roots have their own meanings. They must be identified by keyspace and docset, not by the class name alone.

docs.title: Can a consumer reconstruct a complete MSKU listing from the group alone?
docs.text: No. The group provides shared structure and the list of variation item IDs. The consumer must fetch the corresponding ItemKeyspace item families to obtain each variation's price, quantity, lifecycle, and other item-level state. Conversely, an item alone does not establish the complete group membership.

docs.title: 7. Evidence map
docs.text:
The primary source locations for the walkthrough are:

  • Docset.java - document-set schema abstraction.
  • CoreItemProcessor.java - item keys, six-document insert/upsert, partial mutations, locks, UUID map, PII, and delete paths.
  • DocumentConverter.java - item root and child document construction.
  • ListingConverter.java - SSKU/MSKU classification, variation item creation, and group itemIds construction.
  • CoreItemGroupProcessor.java - group keys and three-document mutations.
  • ItemGroupDocumentConverter.java - group document construction.
  • CoreListingDraftProcessor.java - SSKU/MSKU draft insert, upsert, and delete behavior.
  • DraftDocumentConverter.java - draft root, item, group, description, and compatibility documents.
  • UserListingDraftProcessor.java - active-draft map insert/update/delete.
  • RevisionHistoryNudataClient.java - revision and optional child inserts.
  • RevisionHistoryConstants.java - revision keyspace and docset names.
  • DualWriteProcessor.java and DraftDualWriteProcessor.java - V1-to-V2 routing and asynchronous/ramped behavior.
  • ArchiveItemProcessor.java and ArchiveItemGroupProcessor.java - archive keyspace overrides.
