docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
LDM Name: item

Description: The core listing entity in the Item Domain. Each record represents one eBay listing, containing comprehensive information about title, pricing, category, seller, listing lifecycle, and more.

Primary Key: item_id

docs.title: Fields (228)
docs.text:
item_id LONG

A unique identifier for the listing, generated upon successful creation.

auct_titl STRING

Listing title shown to buyers in search results and on the item page.

subtitle STRING

The listing’s full subtitle text; it can be null if the seller did not provide one

item_desc STRING

Seller-provided item description content encoded in Base64. Decode before displaying or analyzing the description text.

item_desc_lgth_num INTEGER

Length of the encoded item description content.

bin_price_lstg_curncy DOUBLE

Buy It Now price in listing currency in View Item page.

More context

Producer Knowledge

  • Producer Ownership — The team and application that owns and maintains the source data

    • Team Name: SX Inventory Mgmt - Listing Platform Core Services
    • Notification Email: DL-eBay-ListingRedesign@ebay.com
    • OnCall Service: https://ebay-cpt.pagerduty.com/service-directory/$PZMGJDA
    • Service Link: https://cloud.ebay.com/app/detail/crlstngsv/overview

  • Producer Process — How producer applications write data to the source system.

    • Service Name: Core Listing Service
    • Source Code: https://github.corp.ebay.com/SellingDomain/crlstngsv
    • Processes: Core Listing Service produces the listing's Buy It Now price when a seller or authorized eBay workflow creates a fixed-price offer, and updates it when the listing price, promotion, offer configuration, or relist information changes. CLS accepts and stores the resulting listing-currency amount for downstream Item LDM publication. This process does not establish localized buyer pricing, tax, checkout total, or final paid amount.

  • Source Storage — Physical storage information of source data, such as NuDoc keyspace, Oracle db.

    • NuDoc Keyspace Name: ItemKeyspace, ItemGroupKeyspace
    • NuDoc Link: https://qa.cloud.ebay.com/cloud-data/databases/nudocument/keyspaces/ItemKeyspace
    • NuDoc Fields: itemkeyspace.ItemQtyPrice.price.fixedPrice

  • Source Model Design — The data structure written by producer applications, such as source classes.

    • Class: Item.class, ItemGroup.class
    • Field: fixedPrice

  • Change Process — How producer-side changes are released, such as PRs, release notes, schema changes, or standard CI/CD process.

    • 8 releases: https://cloud.ebay.com/app/detail/crlstngsv/ecd?pipelineId=48317243&count=10&pageSize=10&current=1
    • 10 PRs in last month: https://github.corp.ebay.com/SellingDomain/crlstngsv/pulls?q=is%3Apr+

Semantic Knowledge

  • Schema — Entities, fields, data types, primary keys

    • Data Type: double

  • Semantics — Entity and field business definitions

    • Description: Buy It Now price in listing currency in View Item page.

  • Data Lineage (Source → LDM) — How data from source systems is extracted, transformed, and mapped into Logical Data Model (LDM) fields, including key transformation and data-cleaning decisions that turn raw inputs into consumption-ready outputs.

    • Data Flow Summary: Extract itemkeyspace.ItemQtyPrice.fixedPrice from two NuDoc keyspaces (ItemKeyspace and ItemGroupKeyspace) via ZeroETL, covering five docsets. Consolidate into SSKU and MSKU entities, then merge and transform into bin_price_lstg_curncy at the item level. [AI Summary]
    • ETL Code: https://github.corp.ebay.com/jiajsun/dw_lstg_item
    • Data Flow Diagram: https://lucid.app/lucidchart/73cbffe1-905b-415f-a5ca-39c1ecf8ad6b/edit?invitationId=inv_d08689cb-9ea6-43bc-96d8-ff416c09b61f&page=a1vXV8fI_cE.#

  • Data Profiling — Observed data characteristics such as null rate, cardinality, value distribution, sample values.

    • ~6.8B items have an amount greater than 0 (min: 0.01; max: 9,999,999,827,968); all remaining items have an amount of 0.
    • Records with non-zero amounts are mainly distributed across Chinese Auction, Dutch Auction (disabled after 2010), and Auction Personal Offer/Second Chance Offer listings.

  • Data Quality — Data quality rules the data must satisfy.

    • not null
    • not negative
    • Check new listing data for Chinese Auction listings sold through Buy It Now. The bin_price_lstg_curncy value must be greater than 0. 
      SELECT *
FROM GDS.item
WHERE AUCT_TYPE_CODE = 1
  AND BIN_SOLD_UP_FLAG = 1
  AND BIN_PRICE_LSTG_CURNCY = 0
  AND AUCT_END_DT > CURRENT_DATE;

  • Data Availability — Data freshness and delivery SLA

    • Freshness: daily
    • SLA: P99 - 7:00 AM PST, P90 - 4:00 AM PST

Consumption Knowledge

  • Consumption Patterns — Common ways users consume and interpret the data.

    • Normally join with gds.exchanging_rate to convert the amount to USD: gds.item.bin_price_lstg_curncy * gds.exchanging_rate.USD_value.
    • GMV calculation for paid items: Buy It Now amount in USD + shipping fee + tax fee.

  • Adoption — Field-level usage and what business decisions or downstream use cases rely on it.

    • 1,000+ MAU (monthly active users querying this field)
    • Main downstream use cases:
      • CBT seller business and policy analysis — CBT
      • Legal purposes — Legal
      • Reporting changes in listing behavior with respect to price changes and promotions — Dhanesh, Lakshmi

start_price_lstg_curncy DOUBLE

Start price in listing currency. For SIF (Store Inventory Format)/FP (Fixed Price) items, this is the BIN (Buy It Now) price. For auctions/Dutch, it's the opening bid price.

rsrv_price_list_crncy DOUBLE

The lowest price at which the seller is willing to sell the item. StartPrice must be lower than ReservePrice. 0 = no reserve set.

orgnl_price_amt DOUBLE

Original price before a promotional/markdown sale discount. NULL if not a promotional sale listing.

lstg_curncy_id INTEGER

Currency ID used for the listing prices. This ID is a foreign key to the Currency LDM.

qty_avail INTEGER

The number of this item that are initially available for sale.

qty_sold INTEGER

The number of items sold in the listing.

lot_size INTEGER

Number of individual physical items per sale unit.

slr_id LONG

Seller's Oracle user ID associated with the listing. Foreign key to User LDM.

slr_prdct_id_txt STRING

Seller-defined product identifier text (e.g. manufacturer part number/ISBN/UPC). Empty if not provided.

sku_num STRING

Seller's custom, application-specific data associated with the item. Data specified here is stored by eBay with the item for seller but it is not used by eBay in any way.

application_id LONG

Application identifier used by external consumers to identify the application or listing tool associated with listing creation. This ID is a foreign key/code to the application logical data model; join to the Application LDM to get the application name. Common examples include 219527 = BOLT, 290356 = BOLT B2C, 384352 = HELIX, 2828 = File Exchange, 114100 = Auto Relist.

lstg_status_id INTEGER

Listing lifecycle status code. Values: 0 = Live, 1 = Ended, 2 = Admin ended, 3 = Schedule Deleted, 4 = Scheduled.

More context

Producer Knowledge

  • Producer Ownership — The team and application that owns and maintains the source data

    • Team Name: SX Inventory Mgmt - Listing Platform Core Services
    • Notification Email: DL-eBay-ListingRedesign@ebay.com
    • OnCall Service: https://ebay-cpt.pagerduty.com/service-directory/$PZMGJDA
    • Service Link: https://cloud.ebay.com/app/detail/crlstngsv/overview

  • Producer Process — How producer applications write data to the source system.

    • Service Name: Core Listing Service
    • Source Code: https://github.corp.ebay.com/SellingDomain/crlstngsv
    • Processes: Core Listing Service sets or updates this lifecycle code when a listing is created or scheduled, becomes live, ends, is administratively ended, is schedule-deleted, relisted, or corrected through reconciliation. CLS stores the accepted lifecycle state for downstream Item LDM publication. The code describes the listing lifecycle recorded by CLS, not buyer eligibility, search visibility, or checkout availability.

  • Source Storage — Physical storage information of source data, such as NuDoc keyspace, Oracle db.

    • NuDoc Keyspace Name: ItemKeyspace, ItemGroupKeyspace
    • NuDoc Link: https://qa.cloud.ebay.com/cloud-data/databases/nudocument/keyspaces/ItemKeyspace
    • Oracle Table: item_cancelling_pending

  • Source Model Design — The data structure written by producer applications, such as source classes.

    • Class: Item.java (extends BaseItem.java)
    • Java Fields: endReason, endDate, startDate, format, secondChanceItem, isBidsFinalized, duration, isScheduled
    • NuDoc Fields: __ROOT__.endRsn, __ROOT__.lifecycle.endDt, __ROOT__.lifecycle.startDt, __ROOT__.format, __ROOT__.scndChncItm, __ROOT__.bidsFl, __ROOT__.lifecycle.duration, __ROOT__.lifecycle.schdldLstng

  • Change Process — How producer-side changes are released, such as PRs, release notes, schema changes, or standard CI/CD process.

    • 8 releases: https://cloud.ebay.com/app/detail/crlstngsv/ecd?pipelineId=48317243&count=10&pageSize=10&current=1
    • 10 PRs in last month: https://github.corp.ebay.com/SellingDomain/crlstngsv/pulls?q=is%3Apr+

Semantic Knowledge

  • Schema — Entities, fields, data types, primary keys

    • Data Type: integer

  • Semantics — Entity and field business definitions

    • Description: Listing lifecycle status code. Values: 0 = Live, 1 = Ended, 2 = Admin ended, 3 = Schedule Deleted, 4 = Scheduled.

  • Data Lineage (Source → LDM) — How data from source systems is extracted, transformed, and mapped into Logical Data Model (LDM) fields, including key transformation and data-cleaning decisions that turn raw inputs into consumption-ready outputs.

    • Data Flow Summary: Consolidate incremental and archived listing records, then derive the listing status from the source type, end indicators, sale status and dates, and scheduled-listing indicators. Pending cancellation records sourced from the Oracle item_cancelling_pending table are used to identify schedule-deleted listings. Assign archived or admin-ended records to 2, pending cancellations to 3, scheduled listings to 4, ended listings to 1, and remaining listings to 0. The derived status is mapped to lstg_status_id in the Item LDM. [AI Summary]
    • ETL Code: https://github.corp.ebay.com/jiajsun/dw_lstg_item
    • Data Flow Diagram: https://lucid.app/lucidchart/73cbffe1-905b-415f-a5ca-39c1ecf8ad6b/edit?invitationId=inv_d08689cb-9ea6-43bc-96d8-ff416c09b61f&page=a1vXV8fI_cE.#

  • Data Profiling — Observed data characteristics such as null rate, cardinality, value distribution, sample values.

    • Potential values: 0 = Live, 1 = Ended, 2 = Admin ended, 3 = Schedule Deleted, and 4 = Scheduled.
    • Distribution in new listing data: 0: 90%, 1: 5%, 2: 1%, 3: 1%, 4: 3%.

  • Data Quality — Data quality rules the data must satisfy.

    • not null
    • Value must be one of 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4.

Consumption Knowledge

  • Consumption Patterns — Common ways users consume and interpret the data.

    • 2000+ daily queries.
    • Top 1 (~70%): Live inventory scoping filter. Use lstg_status_id = 0. (Use auct_end_dt >= CURRENT_DATE for performance optimization.)
      • Fitment live-listing extract for sellers — defines "currently live."
      • FOD seller experiments — use lstg_status_id = 0 to count each experiment seller's active listings as a metric or feature.
      • Draft-or-live seller segmentation (feeds an SMO marketing ticket) — uses lstg_status_id = 0 to flag sellers with at least one live listing.
      • Tax-category rule audit — uses lstg_status_id = 0 to restrict the tax-category-matching audit to currently live listings only.
    • Top 2 (~10%): Exclusion of not-yet-started listings. Uses lstg_status_id <> 4.
      • Historical seller listing summary — excludes scheduled (not-yet-live) listings while keeping live, ended, and admin-ended listings for trend statistics.

  • Adoption — Field-level usage and what business decisions or downstream use cases rely on it.

    • 1,000+ MAU (monthly active users querying this field)
    • Main downstream use cases:
      • Marketing feeds supporting approximately $1B GMV

auct_type_code INTEGER

Listing format code. Values: 0=Unknown Auction, 1=Chinese Auction/Auction-with-BIN, 2=Dutch Auction, 4=Auction Yankee never implemented, 5=Old Live Auctions deprecated, 6=AdFormat, 7=Store Fixed Price, 8=Second Chance Offer, 9=Fixed Price/GTC, 12=Half.com, 13=Classified Ads/Lead Gen, 14=eBay Express Only, 15=Shopping.com/SDC stopped 2008/8/15

auct_start_dt DATE

Date the listing became (or is scheduled to become) live.

auct_end_dt DATE

Date the listing ended or is scheduled to end.

sale_sched_end_dt DATE

Scheduled end date set at listing creation (start + duration). It is only updated when the seller changes listing duration or sale start date in RYI (Revise Your Item) and there has been no sale.

auct_start_date TIMESTAMP

The timestamp when the listing becomes live

auct_end_date TIMESTAMP

Timestamp the listing ended or is scheduled to end.

site_create_date TIMESTAMP

Date and time the listing was created. This value is read-only and cannot be updated.

last_modfd_dt DATE

Date the listing was last modified on the site.

auction_end_reason_code INTEGER

Reason code for why the listing ended. Values: 0=Natural end/not ended early, 1=Seller-ended: lost or broken, 2=Seller-ended: no longer available, 3=Seller-ended: error in bid/reserve, 4=Seller-ended: listing error, 5=Sold to highest bidder early, 6=EndReasonAVSTickets, 7=SIF Bulk End, 8=Ended by DBA script, 9=SoldOnProStores deprecated, 10=SoldVehicle variant, 11=Ended on zero quantity, 12=SoldVehicle Motors FSBO, 99=GTC renewal failure, -1=invalid, -88=invalid sentinel, -99=pre-2008 unknown.

relist_parent_item_id LONG

Item ID of the parent listing this item was relisted from (via relist or sell-similar). -999=no parent (original listing).

relistid LONG

Indicates if the listing is ended with a relisted one. If it's > 0, it means that the item has been ended and a new relisted one has been created. and the value of this relistId is the same as the value of itemId of the new relisted item

item_vrsn_id LONG

A generated sequence used to track versions for each revision made by the seller

sgnfcnt_rvsn_cnt INTEGER

An item specific count of the number of times it has been significantly revised.

item_site_id INTEGER

eBay site ID where the item was listed. FK to Site LDM.

slr_site_id INTEGER

eBay site ID where the seller account is registered; this can differ from the site where the item is listed.

high_bdr_site_id INTEGER

Registration site ID of the highest bidder for the listing; -999=no bidder.

leaf_categ_id INTEGER

Primary leaf category ID chosen by the seller for the listing. Use with item_site_id to interpret category hierarchy, SAP category, and higher-level category attributes. See Category LDM.

Example:

  • 41931 = Computers & Networking:Software:Education & Reference:Car Repair

leaf_categ_name STRING

Name of the leaf category where the item is listed.

Example:

  • Computers & Networking:Software:Education & Reference:Car Repair

leaf_categ_id2 INTEGER

Secondary leaf category ID chosen by the seller when the listing is posted in two categories; 0 means no secondary category.

meta_categ_id INTEGER

Meta category ID

Example:

  • 58058 = Computers/Tablets & Networking

meta_categ_name STRING

Meta category name (top level)

Example:

  • Computers/Tablets & Networking

categ_lvl2_id INTEGER

Level 2 category ID

Example:

  • 18793 = Software

categ_lvl2_name STRING

Level 2 category name

Example:

  • Software

categ_lvl3_id INTEGER

Level 3 category ID

Example:

  • 3783 = Education, Language, Reference

categ_lvl3_name STRING

Level 3 category name

Example:

Level 4 category ID

Example:

  • 3783 = Education, Language, Reference

categ_lvl4_name STRING

Level 4 category name

Example:

categ_lvl5_id INTEGER

Level 5 category ID

Example:

Level 5 category name

Level 6 category ID

categ_key LONG

Surrogate category hierarchy key for the primary leaf category of the listing.

categ_key2 LONG

Surrogate category hierarchy key for the secondary leaf category of the listing, when a secondary category exists.

categ_move_to_id INTEGER

Replacement category ID when the original leaf category has been retired or moved to another category structure.

stor_categ_id LONG

Primary store category ID under which this listing appears in the seller's eBay Store. 0 = no store category assigned.

stor_categ2_id LONG

Secondary store category ID. 0 = no secondary store category.

sap_category_id INTEGER

Search Annotation Platform (SAP) category ID assigned to the listing.

lcl_sap_categ_name STRING

Local Search Annotation Platform (SAP) category name for the listing category.

glb_sap_categ_name STRING

Global Search Annotation Platform (SAP) category name for the listing category.

bsns_vrtcl_name STRING

Business Vertical Name (e.g. Electronics, Fashion, Motors).

item_cntry_id INTEGER

Unique identifier of the country where the item is physically located, as declared by the seller. Note: reflects item location, not seller registration country (see slr_cntry_id).

slr_cntry_id INTEGER

Country ID where the seller account is registered; this can differ from the physical item location country.

high_bdr_cntry_id INTEGER

Country ID of the highest bidder for the listing; -999=no bidder.

item_loc STRING

Seller-provided textual geographical location of the item.

item_zip STRING

Zip/postal code of item location.

Structured product attributes and eBay-derived catalog/classifier signals, such as brand, MPN, GTIN, aspect values, ePID adoption, and product coverage.

item_cndtn_id INTEGER

Seller-provided item condition code for the listing. Common values include 1000 = New, 1500 = New other, 1750 = New with defects, 2000 = Certified Refurbished, 2500 = Seller refurbished, 2750 = Like new, 3000 = Used / Pre-owned Good, 4000 = Very good, 5000 = Good, 6000 = Acceptable, 7000 = For parts or not working.

cndtn_rollup_id INTEGER

Higher-level item condition rollup derived from the item condition. Values: 1 = New, 2 = Refurbished, 3 = Used, 4 = Unknown; unknown can later resolve when condition attributes are updated.

bold_title STRING

If specified, the seller wants the title for the item's listing to be in boldface type. Applicable listing fees apply. Does not affect the item subtitle (Item.SubTitle), if any. Not applicable to eBay Motors. Values: "0"=not bold, "1"=bold, empty string=legacy historical records not tracked

glry_type_id INTEGER

Indicates the type of gallery image for the listing. Potential values: 0 = no gallery, 1 = standard gallery, 2 = featured gallery, 6 = gallery variant, 7 = super gallery/gallery plus, NULL = not set.

gallery_url STRING

Single gallery image URL for the listing, usually the first picture URL and used in search or merchandising placements.

photo_count INTEGER

Number of photos attached to the listing.

photo_display_type INTEGER

Photo display mode code for the listing. Values: 0=Standard Show, 1=Slide Show, 2=Large Photo Show, 3=Picture Pack, 4=EPS Picture Show, 5=Self Hosted Picture Show, 6=SuperSize Picture Show.

picture_url STRING

URL(s) of the listing's View Item pictures. Multiple URLs may appear semicolon-delimited.

private_yn STRING

Indicates a private listing where bidder identities are hidden. Values: "0" = not private, "1" = private.

super_featured STRING

Super-featured (top-of-category) listing upgrade. Values: "0"=not super-featured, "1"=super-featured, empty string=legacy records.

shipping_fee DOUBLE

First domestic shipping service cost in listing currency as shown on listing. 0 if seller used the shipping calculator. Does not necessarily reflect actual fees paid.

shipping_xfee DOUBLE

Per-additional-item shipping fee shown on listing. Does not necessarily reflect actual fees paid.

shipping_type INTEGER

Shipping cost model selected for the listing. Values include 0 = not specified, 1 = flat rate, 2 = calculated rate, 3 = freight, 5 = flat domestic/calculated international, 6 = calculated domestic/flat international, -999 = null.

package_size INTEGER

Shipping package type code that identifies the package format used to ship the item(s). Values: 0=None/not specified, 4=Package/Thick Envelope, 1=Letter, 26=FedEx Envelope, 5=Large Package, 2=Large Envelope , 19=USPS Large Flat Rate Box, 29=DHL Flyer, 27=FedEx Pak, 21=USPS Flat Rate Envelope, 22=USPS Padded Flat Rate Envelope, 24=USPS Legal Flat Rate Envelope, 17=Irregularly Shaped, 30=DHL Box, 7=UPS Letter.

weight LONG

Item weight in the unit specified by weight_unit_type. 0 = not specified.

weight_unit_type INTEGER

Unit of weight for the item. Values: 1=Pounds, 2=KiloGrams

payment_cash STRING

Indicates whether payment on pickup / cash on pickup is accepted. When used, buyer and seller arrange offline payment and pickup. Values: "0"=no, "1"=yes, empty string=legacy records.

payment_cc STRING

Indicates whether credit card payment is accepted as a payment method for the listing. Values: "0"=no, "1"=yes, empty string=legacy records

payment_moneyxfer STRING

Indicates whether direct money transfer is accepted as a payment method for the listing. Values: "0"=no, "1"=yes, empty string=legacy records.

return_policy_yn STRING

Y/N flag indicating whether the seller entered text in the Payment Instructions field. Values: "N", "Y", empty string(legacy records)

tax_new DOUBLE

Sales tax percentage specified by the seller (e.g. 6.500 = 6.5%). 0 = no seller-specified tax.

tax_new_state STRING

State/region code to which the seller-specified sales tax rate (tax_new) applies. -999=null/not specified.

is_immediate_payment_required INTEGER

Indicates whether immediate payment is required for the listing.

is_buyer_responsible_for_shipping INTEGER

Indicates whether the buyer is responsible for shipping, primarily for Motors listings.

is_tax_applied_to_shipping INTEGER

Indicates whether sales tax applies to the shipping fee for the listing.

has_free_shipping_pre_promo INTEGER

Indicates whether the listing had standard free shipping before a promotional sale.

is_free_shipping_sale INTEGER

Indicates whether the item is on a free-shipping sale promotion.

is_intl_shipping_promotion INTEGER

Indicates whether the item participates in an international shipping promotion.

is_domestic_shipping_promotion INTEGER

Indicates whether the item participates in a domestic shipping promotion.

is_gsp_shipping_enabled INTEGER

Indicates whether Global Shipping Program (GSP) intermediated shipping is enabled for the listing.

is_ebay_managed_shipping_eligible INTEGER

Indicates whether the item is eligible for eBay managed shipping.

is_irregular_package INTEGER

Indicates whether the shipping package is irregular or odd-shaped.

is_managed_shipping_opted_in INTEGER

Indicates whether the seller/listing opted in to managed shipping.

is_merchant_fulfillment_supported INTEGER

Indicates whether merchant fulfillment support / default MSKU price-set fulfillment support is enabled for the listing.

is_amex_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether American Express is accepted as a payment method for the listing.

is_cash_in_person_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether cash-in-person payment is accepted, primarily for Motors listings.

is_cod_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether cash on delivery (COD) is accepted as a payment method.

is_cod_prepay_delivery_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether China-site COD prepay delivery is accepted for the listing.

is_digital_delivery_supported INTEGER

Indicates whether the item supports digital delivery.

is_discover_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether Discover card is accepted as a payment method for the listing.

is_loan_check_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether loan check payment is accepted, primarily for Motors listings.

is_money_order_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether money order or cashier check is accepted as a payment method.

is_other_payment_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether another offline/other payment method is accepted.

is_other_online_payment_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether another online payment method is accepted.

is_paisapay_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether PaisaPay credit card payment is accepted, primarily for eBay India.

is_paisapay_escrow_enabled INTEGER

Indicates whether PaisaPay escrow is enabled.

is_paisapay_escrow_emi_enabled INTEGER

Indicates whether PaisaPay escrow EMI is enabled.

is_payment_in_description INTEGER

Indicates whether payment details are provided in the listing description.

is_paypal_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether PayPal is accepted as a payment method for the listing.

is_personal_check_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether personal check is accepted as a payment method.

is_postal_transfer_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether postal transfer is accepted as a payment method, primarily for China-site listings.

is_prepay_delivery_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether pre-pay delivery is accepted as a payment method, primarily for China-site listings.

is_visa_mc_accepted INTEGER

Indicates whether Visa or MasterCard is accepted as a payment method for the listing.

is_ebay_plus_supported INTEGER

Indicates whether the item supports or requested the eBay Plus program.

eplus_elgbl_ind INTEGER

Indicates whether the item is eligible for the eBay Plus business program.

attr_brand_txt STRING

Brand value tagged by the seller from seller-input item specifics, using attr_id 3982.

at_cnfdnc INTEGER

Auto-tag product reference/ePID adoption method for the item. Examples: 1001 = seller adopted, 1003 = GTIN match, 1004 = Brand + MPN match, 5000-5200 = Hydra, 9000 = manual adoption, 11003 = GTIN match to BEP, 11004 = Brand + MPN match to BEP.

msct_score_num STRING

Miscategorization score for the item; scores >= 70 are treated as miscategorized cases.

mpn_txt STRING

Manufacturer Part Number (MPN) for the item, deduplicated across classification, product information, and seller-provided sources.

upc_txt STRING

Universal Product Code (UPC) for the item, deduplicated across classification, product information, and seller-provided sources.

isbn_txt STRING

docs.title: Get US Listings in a Category
docs.text:
SELECT
    item_id,
    auct_titl             AS title,
    bin_price_lstg_curncy AS price,
    qty_avail,
    item_cndtn_id         AS condition_id,
    slr_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0          -- US site
  AND leaf_categ_id = 9355      -- Cell Phones & Accessories
  AND lstg_status_id = 0        -- Live listings
LIMIT 100;

docs.title: Filter by Condition and Price Range
docs.text:
-- New items within a price range
SELECT
    item_id,
    auct_titl             AS title,
    bin_price_lstg_curncy AS price,
    item_cndtn_id         AS condition_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0          -- US site
  AND item_cndtn_id = 1000      -- 1000 = New
  AND bin_price_lstg_curncy BETWEEN 100 AND 500
  AND lstg_status_id = 0        -- Live listings
ORDER BY bin_price_lstg_curncy ASC
LIMIT 100;

docs.title: Migration Guide
docs.text: How to migrate from legacy Hive tables to Item Domain LDM.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Item Domain LDM consolidates multiple fragmented Hive tables into unified logical entities. This guide helps you migrate existing queries to the new LDM interface.

Benefits of migrating:

  • Simpler queries: Query by business concepts instead of physical table names
  • Better performance: Optimized materialized views on DLS
  • Unified interface: Consistent access pattern across all item-related data
  • Governed data: Standardized, quality-controlled data models

docs.title: Step 1: Identify Your Legacy Sources
docs.text: List the legacy Hive tables and fields used by your current query. Use the reference below to find the corresponding Item Domain LDM entity.

docs.title: Step 2: Check Fields and Replace with LDM Entities
docs.text: Confirm the required fields exist in the target LDM entity, then replace legacy table and field references with the corresponding gds.* LDM entity and LDM fields. Most migrations are table or field substitutions.

docs.title: Step 3: Test and Validate
docs.text: Compare results between legacy and LDM queries to ensure row counts, filters, and key business metrics remain consistent.

docs.title: Basic Item Query
docs.text:
Migrate from DW_LSTG_ITEM to gds.item.

Before (Legacy)After (LDM) 
SELECT 
    item_id,
    auct_titl             AS title,
    bin_price_lstg_curncy AS price,
    leaf_categ_id,
    slr_id,
    item_site_id
FROM DW_LSTG_ITEM
WHERE item_site_id = 0
  AND leaf_categ_id = 58058
  AND auct_end_dt >= CURRENT_DATE
LIMIT 100;

SELECT 
    item_id,
    auct_titl             AS title,
    bin_price_lstg_curncy AS price,
    leaf_categ_id,
    slr_id,
    item_site_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0
  AND leaf_categ_id = 58058
  AND auct_end_dt >= CURRENT_DATE
LIMIT 100;

Changes: - ✅ Replace DW_LSTG_ITEM → gds.item - ✅ Column names remain the same - ✅ WHERE clause unchanged

docs.title: Migrating Flag Fields
docs.text:
In legacy DW tables, many item indicator attributes were packed into bit-level flag columns such as flags, flags2, flags09, flags12, passwrd, passwordex, sale_status, and visitcount. In Item LDM, these decoded flags are exposed directly as individual 0/1 integer columns, so consumers should select the LDM column instead of repeating bitwise logic in every query.

Before (Legacy)After (LDM) 
SELECT
    item_id,
    CASE WHEN (CAST(flags AS BIGINT) & 262144) = 262144 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_seller_on_vacation
FROM DW_LSTG_ITEM;

SELECT
    item_id,
    is_seller_on_vacation
FROM gds.item;

Migration rule: replace each legacy bit extraction expression with the corresponding Item LDM 0/1 indicator column. If your downstream query needs boolean semantics, compare the LDM column to 1 (for example, is_seller_on_vacation = 1).

docs.title: Migration Checklist
docs.text:
Before migrating your queries:

  • Identify all legacy tables used in your current queries
  • Map each legacy table to its corresponding LDM entity
  • Update table references from legacy to gds.* schema
  • Test queries in development environment
  • Validate results match legacy query output
  • Update downstream dependencies (dashboards, reports, pipelines)
  • Document migration for your team

docs.title: Example 1: Basic Item Query
docs.text:
Get basic information for items in a specific category:

SELECT 
    item_id,
    item_title,
    item_price,
    item_quantity,
    seller_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0           -- US site
  AND item_cndtn_id = 1000       -- New condition
LIMIT 100;

docs.title: Modeling Strategy
docs.text: This document explains the unified strategy for identifying entities, attributes, and relationships in Logical Data Model Design.

docs.title: 1. Entity
docs.text: A business object that satisfies the following identification principles:

docs.title: Principle 1: Unique Identifier
docs.text: Has unique identifier that represents individual instance.

docs.title: Principle 2: Independent Lifecycle
docs.text: Can be created, updated, or deleted independently of other entities.

docs.title: Principle 3: Referenced by Multiple Entities
docs.text:
Participates in relationships with multiple entities.

Examples: - ✅ Item - has item_id, independent lifecycle, relates to Variation/Product - ✅ Product - has product_id (ePID), exists independently, referenced by multiple items - ✅ Trait - individual instance referenced by multiple entities

docs.title: 2. Entity Attribute
docs.text:
A property that belongs to and describes a single entity. It has no independent existence outside the entity.

Examples: - item_title - describes Item

docs.title: 3. Relationship
docs.text: A connection between two or more entities. Relationships can be one-to-many (1:N), many-to-one (N:1), or many-to-many (M:N).

docs.title: 1:N (One-to-Many) / N:1 (Many-to-One)
docs.text:
One entity instance can be associated with multiple instances of another entity. Foreign key resides in the "many" side.

Example: Item → Variation 

Item (1) ─────< Variation (N)

One item has multiple variations

docs.title: M:N (Many-to-Many)
docs.text:
Multiple instances on both sides can be associated with each other.

Example: Item ↔ Attribute 

Item (M) >─────< Attribute (N)

An Item can have multiple Attributes
An Attribute can be used by multiple Items

docs.title: 4. Relationship Attribute
docs.text:
A property that belongs to the relationship between two entities, not to either entity alone. It describes the connection, not the entities themselves.

Examples: - photo_count - in Item ↔ Trait mapping, describes how many photos this item has for this trait

docs.title: Step 2: LDM Definition
docs.text: Based on Step 1 identification, define logical data models:

docs.title: Entity → LDM
docs.text:
• Create dedicated LDM for each entity
  • Primary key: entity's unique identifier
  • Fields: entity attributes

docs.title: Relationship → LDM Structure
docs.text:
• 1:N / N:1: Foreign key in the "many" side's LDM
  • M:N:
  • Long-term vision: Query entity LDMs directly, system auto-materializes joins
  • Short-term approach: Create mapping LDM (see Step 3 for details)

docs.title: Relationship Modeling and Querying
docs.text:
1. For 1:N / N:1 Relationships

Query from the "many" side entity:

-- Example: Get variations for an item (1:N)
SELECT 
    v.item_id,
    v.variation_id,
    v.variation_sku,
    v.variation_price
FROM gds.variation v
WHERE v.item_id = 123456789;

2. For M:N Relationships

Current Approach - Pre-joined denormalized mapping tables are modeled as LDM entities for direct consumption:

Relationship Mapping LDM Name Primary Keys Physical Sources Details Item ↔ Attribute Value (Common Attributes) item_common_attribute_value_mapping item_id, attr_id, value_id DW_ATTR_DETAIL_VALUES View Details → Item ↔ Attribute Value (Listing) item_listing_attribute_value_mapping item_id, gcs_id, vcs_id, lstg_attr_id, value_id, value_desc DW_ATTR_LSTG_DTL Item ↔ Attribute Value (Shipment) item_shipment_attribute_value_mapping item_id, gcs_id, vcs_id, shpmt_attr_id, value_id, value_desc DW_ATTR_SHPMT_DTL DW_ATTR_SHPMT_DTL_COLD Item ↔ Attribute Value (Fitment) item_fitment_attribute_value_mapping item_id, auct_end_dt, ftmnt_grp_id, ftmnt_name, ftmnt_value_text, src_ind, cmbntn_grp_id DW_LSTG_ITEM_FTMNT Item ↔ Attribute Value (Tags) item_tag_attribute_value_mapping item_id, gcs_id, vcs_id, lstg_attr_id, tag_name, tag_value_txt DW_ATTR_LSTG_TAG_DTL Item ↔ Attribute Value (Tax) item_tax_attribute_value_mapping item_id, sale_tax_rate, jrsdctn_cntry_id, jrsdctn_tx LSTG_SALE_TAX Item ↔ Picture item_picture_mapping item_id, trait_name LSTG_ITEM_PIC Item ↔ Aspect Value item_aspect_value_mapping item_id, aspect_name, aspect_value_name ITEM_ASPCT_CLSSFCTN_SAP Variation ↔ Aspect Value variation_aspect_value_mapping variation_id, aspect_name, aspect_value_name VRTN_ASPCT_CLSSFCTN_SAP Variation ↔ Trait variation_trait_mapping variation_id, trait_name LSTG_ITEM_VRTN_TRAIT 
-- Example: Get item attributes using mapping table
SELECT 
    i.item_id,
    i.auct_titl AS title,
    m.attr_id,
    m.value_desc
FROM gds.item i
JOIN gds.item_common_attribute_value_mapping m ON i.item_id = m.item_id
WHERE i.item_site_id = 0
  AND m.attr_id = 1000
LIMIT 100;

Future Vision - The long-term vision is to abstract M:N relationships into more intuitive entity-relationship models with dynamic materialization on DDF. This follows the modeling strategy described in this document.

docs.title: Step 3: Physical Source Mapping
docs.text: Map physical Hive tables to LDMs based on table granularity and type.

docs.title: 1. Granularity Analysis
docs.text:
Analyze physical table primary key structure to determine granularity:

  • Single entity key (e.g., item_id) → Entity table
  • Composite key with two entity FKs (e.g., item_id + attr_id) → Relationship table (M:N)
  • Composite key with entity FK + dimensions (e.g., item_id + snapshot_date) → Historical/SCD table
  • Aggregated dimensions (e.g., category_id + date) → Summary table

docs.title: Entity Tables → Entity LDM
docs.text:
Physical tables with entity-level granularity map to entity LDMs.

  • Single source: One physical table → One LDM (e.g., CTLG_PROD_FACT → product)
  • Multi-source: Multiple physical tables → One LDM (e.g., 11 tables → item)
  • Principle: One field has one source table (for given update frequency)
  • Merge complementary attributes from different sources

docs.title: Relationship Tables → Mapping LDM (M:N)
docs.text:
Short-term Approach: Physical M:N tables map directly to mapping LDMs with pre-denormalized attributes.

Mapping LDMs include not just foreign keys, but also denormalized entity attributes and relationship attributes.

Example: dw_attr_detail_values (physical table) → item_common_attribute_value_mapping (mapping LDM) 

-- Physical table structure
item_id, attr_id, value_id, attr_name, value_desc

-- Maps to: Item (M) ↔ Attribute (N)
-- Denormalized: attr_name, value_desc
-- Relationship attributes: none in this case

Benefits: Faster queries, simpler SQL (2-table join instead of 3-table join)

docs.title: SCD2 Tables → Entity/Relationship LDM with Temporal Filtering
docs.text:
Physical SCD2 tables track historical changes over time.

Mapping approach: - Map to corresponding entity or relationship LDM - Add temporal filtering logic in queries

Example: an entity history table with effective start/end timestamps 

-- Current state query
WHERE eff_end_dt IS NULL

-- Point-in-time query  
WHERE snapshot_date BETWEEN eff_start_dt AND eff_end_dt

docs.title: Summary Tables → Typically Not Modeled
docs.text:
Aggregated summary tables contain pre-computed metrics and typically are not modeled as LDMs.

Rationale: - Different granularity (aggregated vs entity-level) - Pre-computed views, not source of truth - Query directly from physical table when needed

Example: CTLG_BRWS_NODE_SD (browse node summary by date) - used as-is, not abstracted into LDM

docs.title: 3. Long-term Vision: DDF Dynamic Materialization
docs.text:
In the future, the platform's Declarative Data Flow (DDF) capability will enable:

  • Dynamic Materialization: Automatically optimize M:N joins based on query patterns
  • Transparent Performance: No manual denormalization needed
  • Simplified Queries: Users query entity LDMs directly, system auto-generates mapping tables

Note: DDF is a long-term roadmap item. For now, use the pre-denormalized mapping LDMs provided.

docs.title: Sample Data vs. Schema Alignment Report
docs.text:
This page documents the findings from cross-checking all 22 raw LDM JSON sample files (under data/sample-data/item-raw-ldm-samples/) against their corresponding schema definition pages in docs/entities/.

Each schema is rated:

  • 🟢 Aligned — data matches schema; no corrections needed
  • 🟡 Partially aligned — content matches but schema documentation has gaps or omissions
  • 🔴 Misaligned — documented field format or name is factually wrong in the schema

docs.title: Critical Corrections (🔴 Must Fix)
docs.text:
Three schemas document primary-key ID generation patterns that do not match actual data. The prefixes are condensed in production; underscores documented in the schema are absent in reality.

Schema Field Documented Format Actual Format itemkeyspace-business-policies.md plcsId BIZ_POL_<itemId> BIZPOL_<itemId> itemkeyspace-item-details.md itemDetailsID ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId> ITEMDET_<itemId> itemkeyspace-item-qty-price.md ItemQtyPriceID QTY_PRICE_<itemId> QTYPRICE_<itemId>

Action: Update the "ID Generation" examples (and the existing review-notes table in ldm-review-notes.md) for these three pages to use the correct prefix strings.

Note: the GroupBusinessPolicies schema inherits its field shape from ItemBusinessPolicies; its plcsId values in sample data use BIZPOL_<groupId>, confirming the same prefix convention applies to the group-level counterpart.

docs.title: 1 — ItemGroupKeyspace / GroupBusinessPolicies
docs.text:
File: ItemGroupKeyspace/GroupBusinessPolicies.json Schema: itemgroupkeyspace-group-business-policies.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (plcsId, retTrms, pmtTrms, shipTrms) are present and correctly structured. The BIZPOL_<groupId> prefix convention used in plcsId is consistent but not explicitly stated in the schema text.

Gap: Schema does not document the BIZPOL_ prefix convention for plcsId.

docs.title: 2 — ItemGroupKeyspace / GroupDescription
docs.text:
File: ItemGroupKeyspace/GroupDescription.json Schema: itemgroupkeyspace-group-description.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

groupDescId, groupDesc, compDesc, and grpDescRevsnDt are all present in samples. Some records omit compDesc entirely (not present, not null); some records omit grpDescRevsnDt. Both are valid optional states.

Gap: Schema does not note that compDesc and grpDescRevsnDt can be absent when no compressed form or revision timestamp exists.

docs.title: 3 — ItemGroupKeyspace / ItemGroupKeyspace_ROOT_
docs.text:
File: ItemGroupKeyspace/ItemGroupKeyspace_ROOT_.json Schema: itemgroupkeyspace-root.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (PK, owner, groupTitle, itemIds, itmsVryBy, imgVryBy, images, grpVrs, grpDrftId, mFulfillmentSprt, globalIdentifiers, httpsCmplt, createdDt, lastmodifiedDt, admEndDt, groupType, sellerGroupKey, compat, cmpCompat) are present and correctly typed.

Observation: Within imgVryBy.trtImg, some trait image entries contain only trtVal with no img key — meaning certain variation trait values have no associated images. This is valid but not called out in the schema description of ImagesVaryBy.

docs.title: 4 — ItemKeyspace / BusinessPolicies
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/BusinessPolicies.json Schema: itemkeyspace-business-policies.md Rating: 🟡 Partially aligned — plcsId prefix is wrong in docs (see Critical Corrections above)

Content fields (retTrms, pmtTrms, shipTrms) are fully aligned. Calculated shipping records correctly carry null for shpCost / addUnitCost with a non-null pkgHndlgCost — this pattern is not explained in the schema.

docs.title: 5 — ItemKeyspace / ItemCompatibility
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemCompatibility.json Schema: itemkeyspace-item-compatibility.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All 10 sample records show compat, cmpCompat, and ftExempt as null. This is correct for non-automotive items that carry no fitment data. The ItemCompID prefix COMPAT_<itemId> is confirmed by the data.

docs.title: 6 — ItemKeyspace / ItemDescription
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemDescription.json Schema: itemkeyspace-item-description.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

ItemDescID, desc, compDesc, and descRevsnDt are all present. Some records omit compDesc entirely; one record has descRevsnDt: null. Both are expected optional states.

Gap: Schema should note that compDesc and descRevsnDt are nullable/optional.

docs.title: 7 — ItemKeyspace / ItemDetails
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemDetails.json Schema: itemkeyspace-item-details.md Rating: 🔴 Misaligned — see Critical Corrections above

Content-wise, itemDetailsID and hasRlxdRls match. Optional fields (fixedPriceHP, strtBidPriceHP, docs, srcLstId) are absent from all samples because the sample items do not require them — this is expected.

docs.title: 8 — ItemKeyspace / ItemKeyspace_ROOT_
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemKeyspace_ROOT_.json Schema: itemkeyspace-root.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

The rich schema (50+ fields) is well-represented in sample data. All major embedded objects (lifecycle, trmsAndPolicies, tax, category, rgltryInfo, vslEncmt, images, aspects, gblIdentifiers) are present and correctly structured.

Undocumented fields found in sample data:

Field in Data Notes pk (lowercase) Appears alongside PK (uppercase) in some records; appears to be a lowercase alias or legacy duplicate images[].extPicUrl External picture URL present in some image entries alongside eBayPicUrl; not in the schema's ImageMap description

docs.title: 9 — ItemKeyspace / ItemLock
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemLock.json Schema: itemkeyspace-item-lock.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (pk, st, qty, expDt, cmtDt, cnclDt, extDt, extCnt, crtDt, modDt, uuid) are present. The summary lock record (LOCK_$$$SUMMARY$$$) uses the same schema with only the aggregate fields populated — consistent with schema documentation.

Observation: The qty field is encoded inconsistently across records: some use {"$numberLong": "1"} (MongoDB extended JSON), others use plain integer 1. Both represent the same value; the schema declares long which is correct in both forms.

docs.title: 10 — ItemKeyspace / ItemQtyPrice
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemQtyPrice.json Schema: itemkeyspace-item-qty-price.md Rating: 🔴 Misaligned — see Critical Corrections above, plus undocumented fields

Beyond the prefix error, two additional fields appear in sample data that are not documented in the schema:

Undocumented Field Observed In Notes lifecycle Ended items (e.g., QTYPRICE_110833294592) Contains endDt and schdldEndDt; represents lifecycle data on items that have ended crLstgDtVrs Some records Core listing data version string; documented in ItemRoot but not in this docset

docs.title: 11 — ItemKeyspace / UuidMap
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/UuidMap.json Schema: itemkeyspace-uuid-map.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

listingId and listingAppId are present and correctly typed. The key shape ($UUIDMAP$_<sellerId>/<uuid> encoded in __key[0].string) matches the schema statement that seller ID and UUID are part of the key shape, not document fields.

docs.title: 12 — ListingDraft / ItemDraft
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ItemDraft.json Schema: listingdraft-item-draft.md Rating: 🟡 Partially aligned — undocumented fields

Content is broadly correct across the rich schema. Two fields present in sample data are absent from the schema's field table:

Undocumented Field Notes origItmId Original item ID from which a Relist or SellSimilar draft was created; critical provenance field invTrkMth Abbreviated form of invntryTrkMthd (inventory tracking method); same semantics as invntryTrkMthd in ItemRoot but with a shortened field name

docs.title: 13 — ListingDraft / ItemDraftCompatibility
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ItemDraftCompatibility.json Schema: listingdraft-item-draft-compatibility.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

DraftCompID, compat (full propertiesList entries with Car Make, Model, Variant, BodyStyle, Plat_Gen, Cars Type, Cars Year, Engine), and cmpCompat (absent when no compressed form) are all consistent with schema.

docs.title: 14 — ListingDraft / ItemGroupDraft
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ItemGroupDraft.json Schema: listingdraft-item-group-draft.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (PK, grpTtl, imgsVryBy, img, itmsVryBy, slrGrpKey, bizPol, grpId) are present. The grpId value of "0" for unpublished drafts is a valid sentinel value. The embedded bizPol.plcsId is null for drafts that have not yet been assigned a policy ID.

docs.title: 15 — ListingDraft / ItemGroupDraftCompatibility
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ItemGroupDraftCompatibility.json Schema: listingdraft-item-group-draft-compatibility.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

DraftCompID and compat (vehicle fitment entries) are present and correct. cmpCompat is absent in samples (expected when no compressed form is written).

docs.title: 16 — ListingDraft / ItemGroupDraftDesc
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ItemGroupDraftDesc.json Schema: listingdraft-item-group-draft-desc.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

PK, groupDesc are consistently present. cmpDesc and grpDescRevsnDt are absent in several records — valid when no compressed description or revision timestamp is stored.

docs.title: 17 — ListingDraft / ListingDraft_ROOT_
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ListingDraft_ROOT_.json Schema: listingdraft-root.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields are present. usgHistDtl correctly carries an array of {name: "CREATE"/"UPDATE"/"PUBLISH", value: "<appId>"} entries. appCstmInfo carries an XML string. Flag fields (fl through fl12, scrtchFl through scrtchFl4) are present as documented.

Observation: itmId is typed List<String> in the schema but appears as null at the root level in some records (rather than an empty list). This is a nullable distinction the schema does not mention.

docs.title: 18 — ListingRevisionKeyspace / ListingRevision
docs.text:
File: ListingRevisionKeyspace/ListingRevision.json Schema: listingrevisionkeyspace-listing-revision.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (rvsdPrptyGrps, vrsnId, appId, sigRevCnt, vrsnCrtd, rvsdDate, updCrLstgVrs) are present and correctly typed. The GUID-style key ("guid": "AAdcK/x3...") for the ListingRevision collection is the NuDocument internal multi-key format, consistent with the schema note that no persisted key field exists on this class. updCrLstgVrs is absent on older revisions where no version was created — expected.

docs.title: 19 — ListingRevisionKeyspace / ListingRevisionDetail
docs.text:
File: ListingRevisionKeyspace/ListingRevisionDetail.json Schema: listingrevisionkeyspace-listing-revision-detail.md Rating: 🟡 Partially aligned — one undocumented field

All core fields (rvsdPrptyGrp, rvsdPrpty, chgTp, newVal, oldVal) are present. lbl is never observed in samples (optional and rarely populated).

Undocumented field:

Field Notes lstRvsnDtlId Appears as {"reference": "<id>"} in some records; appears to be a reference pointer used internally, not exposed as a Java property

docs.title: 20 — ListingRevisionKeyspace / ListingRevisionKeyspace_ROOT_
docs.text:
File: ListingRevisionKeyspace/ListingRevisionKeyspace_ROOT_.json Schema: listingrevisionkeyspace-root.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

lstgId and the TTL-maintenance expiredDate field ({"$date": ...}) are both present. The schema explicitly acknowledges expiredDate as an operational field not declared as a Java property, so its presence in sample data is expected.

docs.title: 21 — ListingRevisionKeyspace / VariationRevisionDetail
docs.text:
File: ListingRevisionKeyspace/VariationRevisionDetail.json Schema: listingrevisionkeyspace-variation-revision-detail.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

varId, rvsdPrptyGrp, rvsdVarPrpty, chgTp, and varTraitVals are all present and correctly structured. newVal and oldVal are absent for itmVarChg/add change-type records — expected, since an addition has no prior value. They are also absent for some binPrc/rvsd records, suggesting these fields are conditionally populated.

docs.title: 22 — UserListingDraft / UserListingDraftMap
docs.text:
File: UserListingDraft/UserListingDraftMap.json Schema: userlistingdraft-user-item-draft-map.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (draftId, mktPlLstdOn, lstgAppId, primCatId, crtMd, eBGenTtl, ttl, imgUrl, stockImgUrl, crtDt, userId, lastModifiedDate) are present and correctly typed.

Undocumented field:

Field Notes ebayGeneratedTitle Appears alongside eBGenTtl in some records as an expanded-name alias (value is always null when present); not documented in the schema field table

docs.title: All Undocumented Fields Across the 22 Schemas
docs.text:
The table below consolidates every field observed in sample data that has no corresponding entry in the schema documentation.

Schema Field Type Notes itemkeyspace-root.md pk (lowercase) String Lowercase alias of PK; appears in same records as the uppercase PK field itemkeyspace-root.md images[].extPicUrl String External (non-eBay) picture URL inside ImageMap; present on some listings itemkeyspace-item-qty-price.md lifecycle Object endDt + schdldEndDt; appears on ended/expired items in the ItemQtyPrice docset itemkeyspace-item-qty-price.md crLstgDtVrs String Core listing data version; documented in ItemRoot but also written to ItemQtyPrice on some paths listingdraft-item-draft.md origItmId String Original item ID for Relist / SellSimilar drafts listingdraft-item-draft.md invTrkMth String (enum) Abbreviated inventory tracking method; same semantics as invntryTrkMthd in ItemRoot listingrevisionkeyspace-listing-revision-detail.md lstRvsnDtlId Object ({reference}) Internal reference pointer; not declared as a Java property userlistingdraft-user-item-draft-map.md ebayGeneratedTitle String Expanded-name alias for eBGenTtl; always null in observed samples

docs.title: Optional Fields That Should Be Called Out as Nullable
docs.text:
Several schemas describe fields without noting that they can be absent or null in practice. The following table lists these, grouped by schema.

Schema Field Observed as null/absent itemgroupkeyspace-group-description.md compDesc Absent when no compressed form itemgroupkeyspace-group-description.md grpDescRevsnDt Absent when no revision timestamp itemkeyspace-item-description.md compDesc Absent or null when no compressed form itemkeyspace-item-description.md descRevsnDt null on some records itemkeyspace-item-details.md fixedPriceHP, strtBidPriceHP, docs, srcLstId Absent when not applicable itemkeyspace-item-qty-price.md minRmntSet, qtySldByPickpStre Never observed; presumed absent when not set listingdraft-item-draft.md docs, srcLstId Absent when not applicable listingdraft-item-group-draft-desc.md cmpDesc, grpDescRevsnDt Absent in multiple records listingdraft-root.md itmId null at root level rather than empty list listingrevisionkeyspace-listing-revision-detail.md lbl Never observed in samples listingrevisionkeyspace-variation-revision-detail.md newVal, oldVal Absent for add-type changes userlistingdraft-user-item-draft-map.md eBGenTtl, stockImgUrl null or absent when not generated

docs.title: Item - Attribute Value Mapping
docs.text: ← Back to Home

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Mapping LDM Name: item_common_attribute_value_mapping

Description: Many-to-many relationship between Items and Attribute Values using the EAV (Entity-Attribute-Value) pattern for basic item attributes.

Primary Keys: item_id, attr_id, value_id

docs.title: Schema Structure
docs.text:
item_id        BIGINT      FK to Item
attr_id        BIGINT      Attribute identifier
attr_name      VARCHAR     Attribute name (denormalized)
value_id       BIGINT      Value identifier
value_desc     VARCHAR     Attribute value (denormalized)

docs.title: Get All Attributes for an Item
docs.text:
SELECT 
    item_id,
    attr_name,
    value_desc
FROM gds.item_common_attribute_value_mapping
WHERE item_id = 123456789;

docs.title: Filter by Specific Attribute
docs.text:
-- Get brand information for items
SELECT 
    item_id,
    attr_name,
    value_desc
FROM gds.item_common_attribute_value_mapping
WHERE item_id IN (123456789, 987654321)
  AND attr_name = 'Brand';

docs.title: Join with Item Entity
docs.text:
-- Get items with specific attribute value
SELECT 
    i.item_id,
    i.item_title,
    i.item_price,
    m.attr_name,
    m.value_desc
FROM gds.item i
JOIN gds.item_common_attribute_value_mapping m ON i.item_id = m.item_id
WHERE i.item_site_id = 0
  AND m.attr_name = 'Brand'
  AND m.value_desc = 'Apple'
LIMIT 100;

docs.title:
-- Get items matching multiple attribute criteria
SELECT 
    i.item_id,
    i.item_title,
    MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Brand' THEN m.value_desc END) AS brand,
    MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Model' THEN m.value_desc END) AS model,
    MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Color' THEN m.value_desc END) AS color
FROM gds.item i
JOIN gds.item_common_attribute_value_mapping m ON i.item_id = m.item_id
WHERE i.item_site_id = 0
  AND m.attr_name IN ('Brand', 'Model', 'Color')
GROUP BY i.item_id, i.item_title
HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Brand' THEN m.value_desc END) = 'Apple'
LIMIT 100;
